translations.text: The vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judea and Jerusalem, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who ruled over Judea.
Listen, heaven, and pay attention, earth, for the Lord has spoken: “I fathered children and raised them up, but they rejected me.”
An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its master's feeding trough, but Israel has not known me, and my people have not recognized me.
Woe to a sinful nation, a people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless children! You have abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
What further blow are you adding to your lawlessness? Every head is distressed, and every heart is sorrowful.
From their feet to their head there is no soundness in them. It is not a wound, nor a bruise, nor an inflamed sore; there is no way to apply a poultice to it, or oil, or bandages.
Your land is desolate, and your cities are burned. Others consume your countryside before your eyes, and it has become desolate, devastated by a foreign people.
The daughter of Zion will be left like a hut in a vineyard, like a shelter for guarding a cucumber field, and like a deserted city.
If the Lord of Hosts had not preserved offspring for us, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.
Listen to the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom! Pay attention to the law of God, people of Gomorrah!
Again, [?] the abundance of your sacrifices to me, says the Lord. I am full of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs, and I do not want the blood of calves and goats.
And when you come to appear before me, who asked you to do these things? You must no longer come to trample my courtyard.

If you bring me fine flour, it is worthless. Your incense is an abomination to me. Your new moons, your Sabbaths, and your great festival day—I will not tolerate them, your fasts, or your days of rest.
And your new moons and your festivals—my soul hates them. I am fed up with you, and I will not forgive your sins.
When you spread out your hands toward me, I will turn my eyes away from you. Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Remove these evil things from your hearts, out of my sight. Stop your wickedness.
Learn to do good. Seek justice. Rescue the oppressed. Give justice to the orphan, and defend the widow's case.
“Come, let us be reconciled with one another,” says the Lord. “Even if your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow. Even if they are like scarlet, I will make them white as wool.”
If you are willing and obey me, you will eat the good things of the land.
But if you are unwilling and do not obey me, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has said these things.
How has the faithful city, Zion, become a prostitute? She was full of justice; righteousness rested within her, but now they have become murderers.
Your silver has been rejected. Your merchants mix water with the wine.
Your rulers are disobedient, partners of thieves. They love gifts and pursue rewards. They do not give justice to orphans, and they pay no attention to the widow’s case.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Woe to the mighty ones of Israel! My anger against those who oppose me will not cease, and I will exact judgment from my enemies.”
I will bring my hand down upon you and refine you to purify you. I will destroy the disobedient and remove all the lawless people within you, along with all the arrogant.
I will establish your judges as at first, and your counselors as in the beginning. After this, you will be called the city of righteousness, the faithful mother city, Zion.
For her captives will be saved through justice, and her return will be through mercy.
The lawless and sinners will be crushed together, and those who abandon the Lord will be wiped out.
For they will be ashamed because of their idols, which they loved, and they were ashamed of their gardens, which they desired.
For they will become like a terebinth tree that has shed its leaves, and like a garden with no water in it.
Their strength will become like a stalk of flax, and their deeds like sparks of fire. The lawless will burn together with the sinners, and there will be no one to put the fire out.
The word that came to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the Lord will become visible, and the house of God will be on the tops of the mountains. It will rise above the hills, and all the nations will come to it.

Many peoples will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and up to the house of the God of Jacob. Let him tell us his way, so that we may walk in it.” For the law comes from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

He will judge among many nations and rebuke a great people. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles. Nation will not take up a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn to wage war.
Now then, you, house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For he abandoned his people, the house of Israel, because their country became full of diviners, like that of the Philistines, as before, and they came to have many children of foreigners.
Their country became full of silver and gold, and their treasures were beyond counting. Their land became full of horses and chariots, and their chariots were beyond counting.
The land became full of abominations, the works of their hands, and they worshiped what their fingers had made.
The man bowed down, and the human being was humbled, and I will not forgive them.
Now go into the rocks and hide yourselves in the earth from the terror of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he rises to shatter the earth.
For the eyes of the Lord are exalted, but the human being is humbled. Human pride will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
For the day of the Lord of Hosts is coming upon everyone who is insolent and proud, and upon everyone who is exalted and lofty, and they will be humbled.
And against every cedar of Lebanon that is tall and flourishing, and against every oak tree of Bashan,
and against every mountain and every high hill,
and against every high tower and every high wall,
and against every ship of the sea and every display of beautiful ships.
Every person will be humbled, human pride will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
And they will hide all their handmade objects,
having carried them into the tombs and the cracks in the rocks and the caves in the earth, away from the terror of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he rises to shatter the earth.
For on that day, a person will throw away his silver and gold abominations, which they made to worship worthless things and bats,
going into the caves in the hard rock and into the crevices of the rocks, away from the terror of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he rises to shatter the earth.
Look! The Lord, the Lord of hosts, will remove from Judea and Jerusalem a strong man and a strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water,
a giant and a powerful man, a warrior and a judge, a prophet and a diviner, and an elder,
and a commander of fifty, a wonderful counselor, a wise architect, and a wise listener.
I will make children their rulers, and mockers will lord it over them.
The people will oppress one another, each person oppressing his neighbor. The young child will defy the old man, and the contemptible person will defy the honored person.
For a man will seize his brother or a member of his father's household, saying, “You have a cloak. Become our leader, and let our food be under your care.”
On that day he will answer and say, “I will not be your leader, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house. I will not be the leader of this people.”
For they will abandon Jerusalem, and Judea has fallen. Their tongues are lawless, and they are faithless toward the things of the Lord, because their glory has now been brought low.

The shame on their faces has testified against them. They have declared their sin and revealed it like the people of Sodom. Woe to their souls, because they have devised an evil plan against themselves!
They say, “Let us bind the righteous man, because he is troublesome to us.” So now they will eat the fruits of the works of their hands.
Woe to the lawless person! Evils will overtake him according to the deeds of his hands.
My people, your tax collectors are destroying you, and those who demand payment rule over you. My people, those who flatter you mislead you and confuse the path of your feet.
But now the Lord is coming for judgment, and he will make his people stand before him for judgment.
The Lord himself is coming for judgment against the elders of the people and their rulers. “Why have you burned my vineyard? The plunder taken from the poor is in your houses.
Why do you oppress my people and shame the faces of the poor?”

These are the things the Lord says: “Because the daughters of Zion have become proud and walk with their necks held high and their eyes making gestures, dragging their robes along the path of their feet and playing with their feet together,
God will bring low the rulers of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will expose their appearance.
On that day the Lord will take away the splendor of their clothing, their ornaments, their chains, their tassels, and their crescent ornaments,
along with their necklaces and the adornment of their faces,
and the arrangement of their splendid ornaments, their hand ornaments, their bracelets, their braids, their razors, their armlets, and their earrings,
and their purple robes and the purple ornaments around their waists,
and the things they put on in their houses, and their sheer Laconian robes,
and their fine linen, their blue-purple cloth, their scarlet cloth, the fine linen adorned with both gold and blue-purple, their veils, and their coverings.

Dust will replace their perfume. Instead of a belt, you will tie on a rope. Instead of gold adornment on the head, they will shave the head because of their deeds. Instead of the purple robe around your waist, you will tie on sackcloth.
Your handsome son, whom you love, will fall by the sword, and your mighty men will fall by the sword and be brought low.
The chests holding your ornaments will mourn. They will leave you alone, and you will be cast down on the ground.
Seven women will take hold of one man, saying, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes. Only let your name be given to us. Take away our disgrace.”
On that day God will appear on the earth with counsel and glory, to exalt and glorify the remnant of Israel.
The remnant that will be in Zion and those left in Jerusalem will be called holy—everyone who has been written in the book for life in Jerusalem.
For the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and he will cleanse the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

He is coming, and every place on Mount Zion and all its surroundings will be shaded by a cloud during the day, and by something resembling smoke and the light of a blazing fire at night. He will shade the whole land.
He will be shade from the heat, a shelter, and a refuge from storm and rain.
He will sing a love song to the beloved about my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a hilltop, in a fertile place.
I surrounded it with a hedge and fenced it with stakes. I planted a vine in Sorek, built a tower in its middle, and dug a winepress in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, then, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more shall I do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, then, I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and it will be plundered. I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will abandon my vineyard. It will not be pruned or dug, and thorns will grow in it like a thicket. I will also command the clouds not to rain on it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the beloved new planting. I waited for it to bring about justice, but it brought about lawlessness; not righteousness, but an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house and bring field next to field, so that they may take [?] from their neighbors. Will you live alone on the earth?
For these things have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts: even if you have many houses, large and beautiful, they will become deserted, with no one living in them.
For the land worked by ten yokes of oxen will produce only one measure of wine, and whoever sows six artabas will get three measures.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink and remain at it until evening, for their wine will make them drunk.
For they drink wine with lyres, a harp, drums, and flutes, but they do not look at God's deeds or examine the works of his hands.
Now, therefore, my people have become captives because they did not know the Lord, and many among them have died because of hunger and thirst for water.
And the underworld has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth to spare no one. The honored, the great, the rich, and the rest of her people will go down.
People will be humbled, the mighty will be disgraced, and haughty eyes will be brought low.
The Lord of hosts will be exalted through judgment, and the holy God will be glorified through righteousness.
Those who were plundered will be pastured like calves, and lambs will eat in the deserted places of those who took them.
Woe to those who drag their sins like a long rope and their lawless deeds like the cord of a calf's yoke.
They say, "Let the one who acts quickly bring near what he is going to do, so that we may see it. And let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know it."
Woe to those who say that evil is good and good is evil, who regard light as darkness and darkness as light, who say that what is bitter is sweet and what is sweet is bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and intelligent in their own sight.
Woe to the mighty who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink.
They acquit the ungodly for a bribe and take away the justice due to the righteous.

Therefore, just as straw is consumed by a fiery coal and burned by a spreading flame, their root will become like chaff, and their blossom will rise like dust. For they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts and provoked the counsel of the Holy One of Israel.

The Lord of hosts became furious with his people. He stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and he struck the mountains. Their corpses became like dung on the road. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still raised.
Therefore, he will raise a signal for the distant nations and draw them from the end of the earth. Look, they are coming swiftly and quickly.
They will not hunger or grow weary. They will not doze or sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
Their arrows are sharp and their bows are drawn. Their horses' hooves are like hard rock, and the wheels of their chariots are like whirlwinds.
They rush forward like lions and stand like lion cubs. He will seize and roar like a wild beast and cast them out, and there will be no one to rescue them.
On that day he will roar because of them, like the sound of the sea with its many waves. They will look up to heaven and down to the earth and find deep darkness—darkness in their hiding place.
In the year when King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord of hosts sitting on a high and lofty throne, and the house was filled with his glory.
Seraphim stood around him, each having six wings. With two each covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
They cried out to one another, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts! The whole earth is filled with his glory.”
The [?] rose up at the sound of their shouting, and the house was filled with smoke.
And I said, “Oh, how miserable I am! I am distressed, because I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among a people with unclean lips. Yet with my own eyes I have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.”
He sent one of the seraphim to me, holding in his hand a burning coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched me with it and said to me, “Look, this has touched your lips. It will take away your lawless deeds and cleanse your sins.”
I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people?” And I said, “Here I am. Send me.”
He said, “Go and tell this people, ‘You will indeed hear, but you will not understand. You will indeed see, but you will not perceive.’

For this people's heart has grown dull. They have become slow to hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, so that they may not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn back, and I would heal them.”
And I said, “How long, Lord?” He said, “Until the cities are devastated so that no one lives in them, and the houses have no people, and the land is [?] a desert.
After these things the Lord will send the people far away, and those who remain will multiply on the earth.
And again, the tenth that remains on it will again be plundered, like a terebinth and like an acorn when it falls out of its casing.”

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to capture it, but they were unable to capture it.
A report was brought to the house of David, saying, “Aram has joined with Ephraim.” His heart and the heart of his people were shaken, as a tree in the field is shaken by the wind.
The Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Jashub, who remained, beside the old pool, on the upper road of the fuller's field.

Tell him, ‘Be careful to remain quiet. Do not be afraid, and do not let your heart grow weak before these two pieces of wood, these smoking torches. For when the fury of my anger comes, I will heal again.’
And the son of Aram and the son of Remaliah, because they have devised an evil plan against you, saying,
‘We will go up to Judea and speak with them and turn them to our side, and we will make the son of Tabeel king over it.’
This is what the Lord of hosts says: “This plan will not stand, nor will it happen.
But the head of Aram is Damascus. In another sixty-five years the kingdom of Ephraim will be destroyed from among the people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe, you will not understand either.”
The Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
“Ask the Lord your God for a sign for yourself, either in the depths or in the heights.”
And Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord to the test.”
And he said, “Listen, then, house of David! Is troubling people a small thing to you? And how can you trouble the Lord?”
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and you will call his name Immanuel.
He will eat butter and honey before he knows how to reject evil and choose good.
Or the evil person will abandon wickedness to choose what is good for himself. They will abandon the land that you fear, so that you will not take it in distress before the two kings.
But God will bring upon you, your people, and your father’s house days that have not come since the day Ephraim removed the king of the Assyrians from Judah.
And on that day the Lord will summon the fly that will rule over a stretch of Egypt’s river, and the honeybee that is in the land of the Assyrians.
And they will all come and settle in the valleys of the land, in the holes in the rocks, in the tombs, in every crevice, and in every tree.
On that day the Lord will shave with the great drunken razor the head of the king of the Assyrians beside the river, along with the hair of his feet, and he will remove his beard.
And on that day a person will raise a young cow and two sheep.
And because of the abundance of milk, everyone who remains on the land will eat butter and honey.
And on that day every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels will become wasteland and thorns.
They will go in there with arrows and bows, because the whole land will become wasteland and thorns.

And they will plow every mountain that is usually plowed. Fear will not come upon that place, for instead of bushes and thorns they will become a grazing place for sheep and a place for cattle to trample.
The Lord said to me, “Take a large scroll of new papyrus and write on it in ordinary human writing: ‘Carry out the plundering of the spoils quickly, for it has drawn near.’”
And appoint reliable witnesses for me: Uriah and Zechariah son of Berechiah.
And he went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, “Call his name ‘Plunder quickly and carry off swiftly.’”
For before the little child knows how to call his father and mother, he will take the power of Damascus and plunder Samaria before the king of the Assyrians.
The Lord spoke to me again.
Because this people does not want the water of Siloam, which flows gently, but you want Rezin and the son of Remaliah as kings over you,
therefore, look, the Lord will bring upon you the mighty and abundant water of the river—the king of the Assyrians and his power. And he will rise over all your valleys and pass over all your banks.
And he will remove from Judea and Jerusalem anyone who has the strength to lift his head or who can complete a task. And his army will fill the breadth of the land. God is with us.
Understand, nations, and be shattered! Listen, as far as the ends of the earth! You who are strong, be shattered! And even if you become strong again, you will be shattered.
And the Lord will destroy the plan you devise, and the word you speak will not stand among you, because the Lord God is with you.
This is what the Lord says: They disobey the strong hand by walking in the way of this people, saying,
“Never let them speak a harsh word to us, for every word this people will speak is harsh.” Do not fear what they fear, and do not be troubled by them.
But the Lord is the one you must regard as holy, and he is the one you must fear.

If you trust in him, he will be a means of purification for you, and you will not stumble against him as against a stumbling stone or a rock that causes a fall. But the house of Jacob is in a trap, and those living in Jerusalem are in a [?].
Therefore many among them will become weak, fall, be broken, and draw near, and the people who are secure will perish.
Then those who seal up the law so that it cannot be learned will be revealed.
And you will say, “I will wait for God, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in him.”
Look, I and the little children God has given me! There will be signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

And if they say to you, “Consult those who call out from the earth and those who speak from within themselves, who say empty things,” are these who call out not like a nation before its god? Why do they consult the dead about the living?
For the law was given as a help, so that they might say, “It is not like this statement, for which there is no way to give a gift.”
And a severe famine is coming upon you. When you become hungry, you will be distressed and speak evil of the ruler and of fatherhood, and they will lift their eyes toward heaven.

And they will look down at the earth, and look! There is affliction, anguish, and darkness, pressing distress and darkness so that they cannot see. And the one in distress will not give up for a time.
Drink this first. Act quickly, region of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, and the rest who live along the coast and on the bank of the Jordan, toward the nations of Judea.
The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light. You who sit in the land and shadow of death—the light will shine upon you.
The greater part of the people whom you brought down in your joy will rejoice before you, like those who rejoice at the harvest and like those who rejoice when they divide plunder among themselves.
For the yoke that was upon them has been removed, along with the rod that was upon their neck. For he has shattered the rod of the one who exacts payment, as on the day when he came against Midian.
For they will give every robe gathered through deceit and every garment as repayment, and they will wish that they had burned them.

For a little child has been born to you; a son has been given to you. His authority rests on his shoulder, and his name will be called “Messenger of the Great Counsel.” For I will bring peace upon the rulers, and salvation to him.

His rule is great, and his peace has no limit. He will sit on David’s throne and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with righteousness, judgment, and mercy, from now and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do these things.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it came upon Israel.
And all the people of Ephraim will know, along with those who live in Samaria, in their arrogance and pride of heart, saying:
The bricks have fallen, but come, let us cut stones, cut down sycamores and cedars, and build ourselves a tower.
God will strike down upon them those who rise up on Mount Zion, and he will scatter the enemies.
Syria from the east and the Greeks from the west, who devour Israel with their whole mouth. Despite all these things, the anger did not turn away, but the hand remained raised.
And the people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
And the Lord removed from Israel head and tail, great and small, in a single day. An elder and one who receives honor—these are the head.
And a prophet who teaches lawless things—this is the tail.
And those who call this people blessed will mislead them, misleading them so that they may swallow them up.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young people, nor will he have mercy on their orphans and widows, because they are all lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks unjustly. Despite all these things, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
And lawlessness has blazed like a fire, and the flame will consume it like dry grass. It will blaze in densely wooded places and consume everything around all the bushes.
Because of the fury of the Lord’s wrath, the whole earth has burned, and the people will be like something burned in a flame, for no one will have mercy on his brother.
But he will bend to the right because he will be hungry, and he will eat on his left, yet the man will not be satisfied as he eats the flesh of his own arm.
For Manasseh will eat Ephraim’s flesh, and Ephraim will eat Manasseh’s, for together they will turn against Judah. Despite all these things, the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still raised.
Woe to those who write wickedness, for they write wickedness as they write.
to deny justice to the poor and rob the needy among the people of their rights, so that a widow becomes their prey and they plunder an orphan.
What will they do on the day of reckoning? For your affliction is coming from far away. To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory,
so that you do not fall into suffering? Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of my wrath and my anger is in their hands.
I will send my wrath against a lawless nation, and I will command my people to take plunder and spoil and to trample the cities, turning them into dust.
But he did not think this way, nor did he consider this in his soul. Instead, his heart is set on destroying great nations.
And if they say to him, “You alone are the ruler,”
he will say, “Did I not take this region above Babylon, and Calneh, the place where they built the tower? And I took Arabia, Damascus, and Samaria.
Just as I took these, I will take all the other regions and their rulers. Cry out, you handmade idols in Jerusalem and Samaria!
For just as I did to Samaria and its handmade idols, so I will also do to Jerusalem.”
And when the Lord has finished doing all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, the Lord will punish the proud heart of the ruler of the Assyrians and the lofty glory of his eyes.
For he said, “I will act by my strength and by the wisdom of my understanding. I will remove the boundaries of the nations and plunder their wealth.

I will shake inhabited cities, and I will take the whole inhabited world in my hand like a nest. I will take them like eggs that have been abandoned, and there will be no one who escapes me or answers me back.”
Can an ax gain glory without the one who uses it to chop? Or can a saw exalt itself without the one who pulls it? This is also like someone lifting up a wooden rod—but it is not so.
But the Lord of hosts will send disgrace upon your honor, and a blazing fire will burn within your glory.
And the light of Israel will become a fire. He will purify him with a blazing fire and consume the multitude like grass.

On that day the mountains will be consumed, along with the hills and the wooded places. He will consume them, from their souls to their flesh, and the one who flees will be like someone fleeing from a blazing flame.
And those who remain among them will be so few in number that a little child can write them down.
And on that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of Jacob will no longer continue to trust those who oppressed them. Instead, they will truly trust in God, the Holy One of Israel.
And the remnant of Jacob will trust in the mighty God.
Even if the people of Israel become like the sand of the sea, it is their remnant that will be saved. For a decree will be fulfilled and cut short in righteousness,
because God will carry out a shortened decree throughout the inhabited world.

Therefore this is what the Lord of Hosts says: “My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians, for he will strike you with a rod. For I will bring a blow upon you so that you see the road to Egypt.”
For in just a little while the wrath will cease, but my anger is coming upon their plan.
God will bring upon them a blow like the blow he brought upon Midian in a place of distress, and his anger upon the road beside the sea, the road that leads to Egypt.
On that day the fear of him will be removed from you, and the yoke from your neck; the yoke will be destroyed and removed from your necks.
For he is coming against the city of Ai.
And he is passing through it toward Megiddo. He will leave his equipment in Michmash, and he is coming through the valley to Agge. Fear will seize Ramah, the city of Saul.
The daughter of Gallim will flee; they will hear him in Anathoth.
And Madmenah has scattered, along with those who live in Gebim.
Plead today with your hands so that they do not remain on the roads. The daughters [?] the mountain of Zion and the hills of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, will throw the honored into confusion with power. He will shatter the lofty with contempt, and those who are high will be humbled.
And they will fall by the axe, and Lebanon will fall along with the lofty.
And a shoot is coming out of the root of Jesse, and a flower is rising from his root.
And the Spirit of God will rest upon him: a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and godliness.
And he will be filled with the spirit of the fear of God. He will not judge according to reputation, nor will he rebuke according to what is said.

But he will judge the case of the humble and rebuke the proud. He will save the humble of the earth and strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath from his lips he will destroy the ungodly person.
And righteousness will be bound around his waist, and truth will be fastened around his sides.
Then a wolf will graze together with a lamb, and a leopard will rest together with a young goat. An ox, a lion, and a calf will graze together, and a little child will tend them.
And a calf and a bear will graze together, and their young will be together with one another. A calf and a lion will eat straw together.
And a little child will put his hand over the snakes’ hole and over the sleeping place of the young snakes.
And they will not bite him, nor will they be able to destroy anything on my holy mountain, because every place is filled with knowledge of the Lord, like abundant water covering the seas.
And on that day there will be the root of Jesse, and the one who will rise to rule the nations. The nations will hope in him, and his resting place will be held in honor.

And on that day the Lord will again reveal his hand to stir up zeal and to honor the remnant of his people that remains among the Assyrians, in Egypt and Babylon, and comes from the Ethiopians and the Elamites, from the regions of the sunrise, and from Arabia.
He will raise a signal for the nations and gather those of Israel who have gone astray. He will gather the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim’s jealousy will be removed, and Judah’s enemies will perish. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not oppress Ephraim.

And they will sail in the ships of the Philistines, plundering the sea together, as well as those in the regions of the sunrise and Edom. They will first lay their hands on Moab, and the Ammonites will be the first to obey.

And the Lord will turn the sea of Egypt into a desert, and he will bring his hand against the river with a violent wind. He will strike the seven valleys of Egypt, so that people can walk through them in sandals.
And there will be a road for the people who remain in Egypt, and it will be for Israel as it was on the day when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And he will say on that day, “I will praise you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned your anger away from me and had mercy on me.”
Look, God, the Lord, is my Savior. I will trust in him, and I will be saved through him. I will not be afraid, because the Lord is my glory and my praise; he has become my Savior.
Draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.
And on that day you will say: Praise the Lord; call upon his name. Proclaim his glorious deeds among the nations. Remember that his name has been exalted.
Praise the name of the Lord, because he has done great deeds. Proclaim these throughout the whole earth.
Rejoice and be glad, you who live in Zion, because the Holy One of Israel is exalted in her midst.
The vision concerning Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a signal on an open mountain. Raise your voices; do not be afraid. Beckon with your hands. Open up, rulers!

I am the one who will give the command, and I am the one who will bring them; they are purified. And I am the one who will bring them. Giants are coming against you in my anger, rejoicing and mocking together.
The sound of the many nations on the mountains, of great crowds of nations! The noise of kings and nations gathering together! The Lord of Hosts has commanded a nation of armed warriors
to come from a distant land, from the farthest edge of heaven’s foundation—the Lord and his armed warriors—to destroy the inhabited world.
Wail, for the day of the Lord has drawn near, and destruction is coming from God.
Therefore every hand will go limp, and every human soul will grow weak.
The elders will be troubled, and pains will seize them like a woman about to give birth. They will be distressed before one another and will be astonished, and their faces will burn like a flame.
For look, the day of the Lord God is coming, without relief, in anger and wrath, to make the inhabited world a wilderness and destroy the sinners upon it.
For the stars of heaven, Orion, and all the heavenly array will not give their light. They will grow dark while the sun is out, and the moon will not give its light.
I will command disasters against the whole inhabited world, and against the ungodly for their sins. I will destroy the arrogance of the lawless and humble the arrogance of the proud.
Those who survive will be more precious than fine gold, and a person will be more precious than a stone from Ophir.
For heaven will grow dark, and the earth will shake from its foundations because of the furious wrath of the Lord of Hosts, on the day when his anger comes.

Those who remain will be like a fleeing gazelle and like a wandering sheep, with no one to gather them in, so that each person will return to his own people and each person will flee to his own country.
For whoever is caught will be brought low, and those gathered together will fall by the sword.
Their children will be torn apart before their eyes. Their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be taken.
Look, I will stir up the Medes against you, who do not value silver and have no use for gold.
They will shatter the bows of the young men and will not spare your children, nor will their eyes have pity on a child.
And Babylon, which is called honored by the kings of the Chaldeans, will become like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
No one will live in it forever, nor will anyone enter it with a great army. No Arab will enter it, and shepherds will not rest there.
Wild beasts will rest there, and the houses will be filled with noise. Sirens will rest there, and demons will dance there.
Donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and snakes will give birth in their houses. Look, he is coming and will not delay.
And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob and choose Israel again. They will rest on their own land, and the foreigner will run to them and join the house of Jacob.

The nations will take them and bring them into their own place, and they will inherit it. They will multiply on God’s land as male and female slaves. Those who took them captive will become captives, and they will rule over those who ruled over them.
And on that day God will give you rest from your distress, from your anger, and from the harsh slavery in which you served them.
And you will take up this lament against the king of Babylon and say on that day, “How the oppressor has come to rest! The troublemaker has come to rest!”
God has shattered the yoke of the wicked one, the yoke of the rulers.
He struck a nation in anger with an incurable blow. He struck a nation with an angry blow and showed no pity. The confident one has come to rest.
The whole earth cries out with joy.
And the trees of Lebanon rejoiced over you, along with the cedar of Lebanon: “Since you lay down, the one who cuts us down has not risen.”
Hades below was stirred up when it met you. All the giants who ruled the earth rose because of you, rising from their thrones. All the kings of the nations lay down in honor, each in his own house.
They will all answer and say to you, “You too have been destroyed like us, and you have been counted among us.”
Your glory has gone down to the underworld, along with your abundant rejoicing. Worms will be spread beneath you, and maggots will cover you.
How has the morning star fallen from heaven! The one who rises at dawn has been shattered to the ground, the one who sends to all the nations.
But you said in your heart, “I will go up to heaven. I will place my throne above the stars of heaven. I will sit on the high mountain, above the high mountains of the north.
I will climb above the clouds. I will become like the Most High.”
But now you will go down to the underworld and to the foundations of the earth.
Those who see you will be amazed at you and say, “Is this the man who makes the earth angry and shakes kings,
who made the whole inhabited world a desert and demolished its cities, but did not release those in chains?”
All the kings of the nations have lain down in honor, each in his own house.

But you will be thrown into the mountains like a loathsome corpse, along with a multitude of dead people pierced by the sword, going down to the underworld. For just as a garment stained with blood cannot become clean,
so it is with you: you will not become clean, because you destroyed the land and killed my people. You will not endure forever, offspring of the wicked.
Prepare your children for slaughter because of your father’s sins, so that they will not rise up, inherit the earth, and fill the earth with war.
“And I will rise against them,” says the Lord of hosts. “I will destroy their name, their survivors, and their offspring.” These are the things the Lord says:
“I will make Babylon a desert, so that hedgehogs will live there. It will become nothing, and I will make it a muddy pit for destruction.”
These are the things the Lord God of hosts says: “As I have said, so it will happen, and as I have planned, so it will stand:
to destroy the Assyrians from the land and from my mountains. They will be trampled. Their yoke will be taken off them, and their glory will be taken off necks.”
This is the plan the Lord has devised for the whole inhabited world, and this is the hand raised over all the nations of the inhabited world.
For who will scatter what the holy God has planned? And who will turn back the raised hand?
In the year in which King Ahaz died, this message came:

“Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, because the yoke of the one who strikes you has been broken. For young snakes are coming from the offspring of snakes, and their young are coming out as flying snakes.
The poor will be fed through him, and poor people will rest in peace. But he will destroy your offspring by famine, and he will destroy your survivors.
Cry out, gates of the cities! Let the trembling cities cry out, all you Philistines, because smoke is coming from the north, and there is no way for you to stand firm.”
And what will the kings of the nations say? “The Lord will lay the foundations of Zion, and the humble among the people will be saved through him.”
The message concerning Moab. Moab will be destroyed in the night, for the wall of Moab will be destroyed in the night.
Sorrow upon you! For Dibon will be destroyed, the place where your altars are. You will go there to weep. Cry out over Nebo in the land of Moab, for every head will be bald and every arm cut.
Put on sackcloth in its squares, beat your breasts on its rooftops, and all of you cry out with weeping in its streets.
For Heshbon cried out and spoke until they heard her voice. Therefore the loins of Moab cry out; her soul will know.

The heart of Moab cries out within her as far as Zoar, for she is a three-year-old heifer. On the ascent to you they come up weeping, on the road to Horonaim, as destruction and an earthquake cry out.
The water of Nimrim will dry up, and its grass will wither, for from now on no grass will be green.
Will she really be saved even this way? I will bring Arabs into the valley, and they will seize it.
For my cry has reached the border of Moab, as far as Eglaim, and its cry as far as the well of Elim.
The waters of Rimmon will be filled with blood, for I will bring Arabs upon Rimmon. I will take away the offspring of Moab, together with Ariel, the remnant of Admah.
For I will send them over the land like reptiles. Is Mount Zion a rock in the wilderness?
For you, daughter of Moab, will be like a bird that has flown away and whose young have been taken. Then, Arnon,
Think very carefully; make her a covering of mourning. At all times they flee in midday darkness. They have divided her; do not be troubled.
The fugitives of Moab will dwell with you. They will be a shelter for you from those pursuing you, because their salt has been taken away, and the ruler has destroyed the one trampling upon the land.
The throne will be established with mercy, and he will sit upon it faithfully, under David's shelter, judging, seeking justice, and acting swiftly in righteousness.
We have heard of Moab's insolence; he is very insolent. I have taken away his arrogance. Your [?] is not like this; it is not like this.
Moab cries out. They all shout throughout the whole land of Moab. You will think about the others who dwell in Desem, and you will not be ashamed before them.

The fields of Heshbon and the vine of Sibmah will mourn, swallowing the nations. You will trample her vines. You will not reach as far as Jazer. Wander in the wilderness. They have abandoned those who were sent, for they crossed the sea.
Therefore I will weep like the weeping of Jazer over the vine of Sibmah. Heshbon produced a tree, and she spoke again: "I will trample their harvest and their vintage, and they will all fall."
Joy and rejoicing will be taken away from their vineyard. They will not rejoice in the vineyards, nor will they press wine into vats, for it has ceased.
Therefore the heart will cry out like a harp over Moab, and my innermost parts like the wall that you made new.
And you will be put to shame, because Moab has worn himself out at his altars. He will enter his handmade shrines to pray, but they will not be able to save him.
This is the word that the Lord spoke against Moab, just as he said it.
Now he says again: "Within three years, counted as a hired worker's days, Moab's glory will be disgraced in all its abundant wealth, and he will become insignificant and without honor."
The message concerning Damascus. Look! Damascus will be removed from among the cities, and it will become a ruin,
abandoned forever as a sheepfold and a resting place for cattle. From now on there will be no one pursuing it.

From now on it will no longer stand high for Ephraim to flee there, and from now on there will be no kingdom in Damascus. The remaining Assyrians will also perish, for you were not better than the children of Israel and their glory.
This is what the Lord God says: "On that day Jacob's glory will diminish, and the abundance of their glory will be shaken.
It will be like someone gathering a ripened harvest and gathering the grain from the ears. It will be like someone gathering ears of grain in a rugged valley,
with a remnant left in it, or like two or three olives on a [?] branch, or four or five left on their branches." This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says:
"On that day a person will trust the one who made them, and their eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.

They will not put their trust in those who took them by force, nor in their [?], nor in the works of their hands that their fingers made. Instead, they will trust the Holy One of Israel, and they will not look to their trees or their abominations.
On that day their cities will be abandoned, just as the Amorites and the Hivites abandoned theirs before the children of Israel, and they will become a wilderness."
Because you have abandoned your God, your Savior, and have not remembered your Lord, you will therefore plant an unfaithful planting, and your seed will be faithless.
But you will go astray on the day when you plant it. If you sow it in the morning, it will bring its harvest to an end on the day when it comes to an end, and as a father divides among his children.
Woe to the multitude of nations that roar like the sea making waves! This is how you will be thrown into confusion, and the rising multitude of nations will cry out

like abundant water rushing violently. He will scatter them and pursue them far away, like the dust of straw from those who thresh before the wind, and like dust from a wheel carried away by a whirlwind.
At evening there will be sorrow; before dawn it will no longer exist. This is the portion of those who plundered you, and the inheritance of those who took possession of you.
Woe to the wings of the ships of the land along the rivers of the Ethiopians,

which sends messengers by sea and written letters over the water. For the scouts will travel swiftly to a tall nation and a foreign people, a powerful nation without hope, which has now been humbled. All the rivers of the land
will be like an inhabited country. Their country will be inhabited like a signal raised on a mountain, and they will hear it like the sound of a trumpet.
For this is what the Lord said to me: “There will be security in my city, like the light of the heat at noon, like a cloud of dew on the day of harvest.

It will happen before the harvest, when the flowers have fallen and the unripe grapes have appeared. He will bring the unripe grapes to an end, prune small branches with sickles, cut off their shoots, and chop them up.
He will leave them together for the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth. All the birds of the sky will gather over them, and all the wild animals of the earth will come upon it.”

On that day gifts will be brought up to the Lord of Hosts from an afflicted people who are being stripped, and from a great people, from now until forever: a faithful and humbled nation on the other side of the river of the land of Egypt, to the place upon which the name of the Lord of Hosts has been pronounced, Mount Zion.
The vision concerning Egypt. Look, the Lord is sitting on a swift cloud and is coming down to Egypt. All the handmade idols of Egypt will shake before him, and their hearts will melt within them.
Egyptians will rise against Egyptians. Each person will fight against his brother, and each person against his neighbor. City will rise against city, and district against district.

The spirit of the Egyptians will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will consult their gods and their idols, those who call out from the earth, and those who speak from within their bellies.
I will deliver Egypt into the hands of harsh masters, and harsh kings will rule over them. These are the things that the Lord God of Hosts says.
The Egyptians will drink the water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.
The rivers will fail, along with the river’s canals. Every collection of water will dry up, and every growth of reeds and rushes
and all the green vegetation surrounding the river will dry up. Everything sown beside the water will dry up in a scorching wind.
The fishermen will groan. All who cast hooks into the river will groan, along with those who throw nets, and those who cast fishing nets will mourn.
Shame will seize those who work with combed flax and those who work with fine linen.
Those who weave them will be in anguish, and all who make beer will grieve and be distressed in their hearts.

The rulers of Zoan will become foolish. The king’s wise counselors and their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are children of wise men, children of kings from ancient times”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them inform you and tell you. Let them understand what the Lord of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
The rulers of Zoan have failed and have been put to shame, and the rulers of Memphis have been disgraced. They will lead Egypt astray, tribe by tribe.
For the Lord has mixed a spirit of confusion for them, and they have led Egypt astray in all their deeds, just as someone who is drunk and vomiting staggers.
And there will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce head or tail, beginning or end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women, in fear and trembling before the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he will bring down upon them.
And the land of the Jews will become a terror to the Egyptians. Whenever anyone mentions its name to them, they will be afraid because of the plan that the Lord has devised against it.
On that day there will be five cities in Egypt speaking the language of the Canaanites and swearing by the Lord’s name. One city will be called Asedek.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians, and a pillar to the Lord at its border.

And it will be an everlasting sign to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians, because they will cry out to the Lord God because of those who oppress them. And the Lord will send them a man who will rescue them; he will rescue them by administering justice.
And the Lord will reveal himself to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will fear the Lord on that day. They will offer sacrifices and make vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
And the Lord will strike the Egyptians with a blow and bring them healing. They will return to the Lord, and he will listen to them and heal them.
On that day there will be a road from Egypt to the Assyrians. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians will go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be a third alongside the Assyrians and the Egyptians, blessed on the earth.
The Lord of hosts has blessed it, saying, “My people who are in Egypt and among the Assyrians will be blessed, together with Israel, my inheritance.”
In the year when Nathan entered Ashdod, after he had been sent by Arnai, the king of the Assyrians, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.
Then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go and remove the sackcloth from your waist, and untie your sandal from your feet. Do this: walk naked and barefoot.”
And the Lord said, “Just as Isaiah my servant has walked naked and barefoot for three years, there will be signs and wonders among the Egyptians and the Ethiopians, and they will understand
that this is how the king of the Assyrians will lead away the captives of Egypt and the Ethiopians, old people and young children, naked, with nothing on their feet, exposing the shame of Egypt.
And the Egyptians will be ashamed because of the Ethiopians, in whom they placed their hope, those whom the Egyptians trusted and who were their glory.
And those who live on this coast will say, “Look! We were placing our hope in them, fleeing to them for help, but they could not rescue us from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, will we escape?”
The message concerning the desert. Like a wind through a desert, [?] coming out of the desert, coming out of the land.

The vision is terrifying, and a harsh matter was told to me: the one who betrays will betray, and the one who acts lawlessly will act lawlessly against me. The Elamites and the envoys of the king of the Persians are coming against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself,
because my waist is filled with pain, and pangs have seized me like those of a woman giving birth. I suffered violence and did not hear; I was distressed so that I could not see.
My heart went astray, and my lawlessness overwhelmed me. My soul fell into terror.
Prepare a table. Drink, eat. Rise, rulers; prepare [?].
For this is what the Lord said to me: “Go and station a watchman for yourself, and report what you see.”
And I saw two horse riders, a donkey rider, and a camel rider. Listen to a great message.
And call Uriah at the Lord’s time. And he said, “I stood all day over the camp; I stood all night.”
And look! He is coming, riding on a chariot. And he answered, saying, “Babylon has fallen, and all its idols and all its handmade images have been shattered on the ground.”
Listen, you who remain! Pay attention, you whose hearts are troubled! I heard a voice from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. He told you:
The vision concerning Idumea. Someone calls to me from Seir. Say, “Why are you crying out? Keep watch at the watchposts.”
Keep watch in the morning and at night. If you inquire, inquire, and stay near me.
He will sleep in the forest in the evening, in Dedan.
Bring water to meet the thirsty person. Meet the fugitive with bread, you who live in the land of Tema.

Because of the multitude of fugitives and the multitude of those who wander, and because of the multitude of swords, and because of the multitude of drawn bows, and because of the multitude of those who have fallen in battle.
For this is what the Lord told me: “Within another year, measured like a hired worker’s year, the glory of the children of Kedar will come to an end.”
And the remaining strong bows of the descendants of Kedar will become fewer, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.
The vision concerning the valley of Zion. What has happened to you, that now you have all gone up onto empty rooftops?
The city was filled with people crying out, “Stop!” Your slain were not slain by the sword, and your dead did not die in battle.
All your rulers fled, and those who were captured were tightly bound. Those whose hearts were melting fled far away.
Therefore I said, “Leave me alone to weep bitterly. Do not exert yourselves trying to comfort me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
For it is a day of turmoil and destruction, of trampling and wandering, from the Lord of hosts in the valley of Zion. They wander, from the least to the greatest; they wander on the mountains.
The Elamites took their weapons for shooting arrows. Men mounted horses, together with the force assembled for battle.
Your finest valleys will be filled with chariots, and horses will block your gates.
They will cover the gates of Judah, and on that day they will look at the finest houses of the city.
They will uncover the things hidden in the houses of David’s fortress. They saw that these were numerous, and that they had diverted the water of the old pool into the city.
And that they had demolished the houses of Jerusalem to strengthen the city wall.

You made a water supply for yourselves between the two walls, inside the old pool. But you did not look up to the one who made it from the beginning, and you did not regard the one who created it, the Lord.
On that day the Lord of hosts called for weeping and mourning, for shaving the head and putting on sackcloth.
But they celebrated with joy and gladness, slaughtering cattle and killing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die.”
This was revealed in the hearing of the Lord of hosts: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”
The Lord said to me, “Go to the chamber, to Shebna the treasurer, and say to him:
‘What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you have dug yourself a tomb here? You have made a tomb on a height and carved yourself a dwelling in the rock.
Look! The Lord God will cast out and crush the man, and he will take away your robe and your glorious crown.
He will throw you into a vast, boundless land, and you will die there. He will make your fine chariot a disgrace and your master’s house a humiliation.
You will be removed from your stewardship and from your possessions.
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah.

I will dress him in your robe and give him your crown. I will place your authority and your administration in his hands, and he will be like a father to those who live in Jerusalem and those who live in Judah.
I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, and there will be no one to contradict him.
I will establish him as a ruler in a secure place, and he will become a glorious throne for his father’s house.
And everyone honored in his father’s house will trust in him, from the least to the greatest, and they will hang upon him.

On that day, this is what the Lord of hosts says: The man established in a secure place will be shaken. He will fall and be taken away, and the glory resting on him will fall, for the Lord has spoken.
The message concerning Tyre. Cry out, ships of Carthage, for they have been destroyed and will no longer be able to come. They brought captives out of the land of the [?].
Whom have those who live on this island come to resemble—the merchants of Phoenicia who cross the sea?
They do business on many waters. The seed of the merchants is like a harvest being gathered in, [?] the merchants of the nations.
The sea said, “Be ashamed, Sidon!” The strength of the sea said, “I have not gone into labor or given birth. I have not brought up children or raised a virgin.”
When Egypt hears this, anguish will seize them because of Tyre.
Go to Carthage! Wail, you who live on this island!
Was this not your arrogance from the beginning, before it was handed over?
Who planned these things against Tyre? Is she insignificant? Were her merchants not powerful? Her honored men are the rulers of the earth.
The Lord of hosts planned to put an end to all the arrogance of those held in honor and to disgrace all their prestige on the earth.
Work your land, for the ships will not be able to come from Carthage.
So your hand will have no power over the sea, which troubles kings. The Lord of hosts has commanded that Canaan’s strength be destroyed.
They will say, “You will no longer continue [?] committing violence and disgracing the daughter of Zion. Even if you go to Kittim, there will be no rest for you there.”
And as for the land of the Chaldeans, this too has been laid waste by the Assyrians. There will be no rest for you there either, for its wall has fallen.
Wail, ships of Carthage, for your stronghold has been destroyed!
On that day, Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the span of a king’s life and like the span of a person’s life. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a prostitute’s song.
Take a harp and go around the city, forgotten prostitute. Play the harp well; sing a great deal, so that they may be remembered.
After seventy years, God will visit Tyre and restore her to her former state. She will become a trading place for all the kingdoms of the inhabited world.

Her trading profits and her wages will be holy to the Lord. They will not store them up for themselves. Rather, all her trading profits will belong to those who live before the Lord in Jerusalem, for eating, drinking, and having their fill, as a contribution for remembrance before the Lord.
Look! The Lord will destroy the inhabited world and make it a desert. He will lay its surface bare and scatter those who live in it.
The people will be like the priest, the male slave like his master, and the female slave like her mistress; the buyer like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the creditor like the debtor.
The earth will be utterly destroyed. The earth will be laid waste through plunder; they will plunder the earth, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
The earth mourned, and the inhabited world was destroyed. The weary people of the earth mourned.
The earth became lawless because of those who live in it, for they abandoned the law and changed the decrees—my everlasting covenant.
Therefore the curse will devour the earth, because those who live in it have mourned. Therefore those who live on the earth will become poor, and few people will remain.
The wine will mourn. All who rejoice in their souls will sigh.
The joy of the tambourines has ceased. Cruelty has ceased, and the wealth of the ungodly has ceased. The sound of the harp has ceased.
They were ashamed and did not drink wine. Strong drink became bitter to those who drank it.
Every city has become deserted. He will shut the house so that no one enters it.
Cry out everywhere over the wine! All the joy of the earth has ended.
The cities will be left deserted, and the abandoned houses will be destroyed.
All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations, as when someone shakes an olive tree. This is how they will be shaken, and when the harvest ends.
These will cry out aloud. But those who remain on the earth will rejoice together with the glory of the Lord. The water of the sea will be disturbed.
Therefore the glory of the Lord will be on the islands of the sea. The name of the Lord will be honored.
The Lord, the God of Israel. From the ends of the earth we have heard wonders. There is hope for the godly, and they will say, “Woe to those who reject, those who reject the law!”
Terror, a pit, and a trap are coming upon you who live on the earth.

And it will happen that whoever escapes the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever comes up out of the pit will be caught in the snare, because openings have been opened in heaven, and the foundations of the earth will shake.
The earth will shake violently; the earth will break apart.
The earth has tilted and shaken like a watchman's shelter, like someone who is drunk and staggering. It will fall and be unable to rise, for lawlessness has prevailed over it.
And God will bring his hand down upon the host of heaven and upon the kings of the earth.
They will gather them together and confine them in dungeons and places of imprisonment. After many generations they will be visited.
The brickwork will dissolve and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem and receive glory before the elders.
Lord God, I will glorify you and bless your name, because you have done wonders—an ancient and true plan that will belong to the Lord.
For you have reduced cities to earth, lofty cities, making their foundations fall. The cities of the ungodly will never be rebuilt.
Therefore the poor people will bless you, and the cities of violent people will bless you.

For you have become a helper to every humbled city and a shade for those distressed by the heat. You will rescue them from wicked people, a shade for those who are thirsty. And the spirit of violent people will bless you.
Like fainthearted people who thirst in Zion because of the wicked and ungodly people into whose hands you handed us.
And the Lord God of hosts will provide for all the nations. They will drink with joy on this mountain; they will drink wine.
And they will anoint themselves with ointment on this mountain. Give these things to all the nations as a gift, for this plan is coming upon all the nations.

Death has been swallowed up after prevailing. And God has also wiped every tear from every face. God has removed the disgrace of my people throughout the whole earth, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
And on that day they will say, “Look, this is the Lord our God, in whom we placed our hope. We have rejoiced, and we will be glad in his salvation.”
God will give rest on this mountain, and Moab will be trampled as a threshing floor is trampled by wagons.
And he will stretch out his hands, just as he himself humbled himself to destruction, and he will humble the arrogance with which he set his hand against him.
And he will bring down the height of the refuge of his wall, and they will come down to the ground.
On that day they will sing this song in the land of Idumea, saying: Look, the lofty city! He will establish a wall and an outer wall for our salvation.
Open the gates. Let the people enter who uphold righteousness and uphold truth,
who trust in truth and preserve peace.
For they have put their hope in you, Lord, forever, the great God forever.
You brought down those who live in high places; you humbled them. You will bring down the lofty cities, and you will bring them down to the ground.
And the feet of the meek will trample them, along with those of the humble.
The path of the godly has become straight, and the path of the godly is prepared.
For the Lord’s path is judgment. We have hoped in his name and in his remembrance,
which our soul desires. My spirit will rise early; from the night it will rise early toward you, God, because your commands are lights upon the earth.

For the ungodly person has withered, along with everyone who does not learn to practice righteousness on earth and act truthfully. Let the ungodly person be taken away, so that he will not see the glory of God.
Lord God, your arm is raised high, but they did not know it. When they understand, however, they will be ashamed. Jealousy will seize an uninstructed people; now fire will devour the enemies.
Lord God, give us peace. You have repaid us according to our deeds.
Lord our God, take us for yourself. We know no one apart from you; we proclaim your name.
But the dead will not see life, and the physicians will not rise. Therefore you brought disaster upon them and destroyed them, and you removed every male of theirs.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evil to all the honored people of the earth.
Lord, I remembered you in distress. Your discipline became a little distress for me.
And like a woman in labor who is close to giving birth and cries out because of her labor pains, so we have become to your beloved because of fear of you, Lord.
We conceived, we suffered labor pains, and we gave birth. You made a spirit of salvation upon the earth, but those who live upon the earth will fall.
The dead will rise, along with those in the tombs, and those in the earth will rejoice. For the dew that comes from you is healing for them, but the land of the ungodly will fall.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your door. Hide for a little while, until the Lord’s anger passes.
For look, the Lord will bring his anger out from the holy place against those who live upon the earth. And the earth will reveal its blood and will not conceal those who have been killed.
On that day God will bring the great, holy, and mighty sword against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and he will kill the dragon.
On that day a beautiful vineyard is something to be desired; begin singing about it.
I am a lofty city, a city under siege. I will water it at dawn, for it will be destroyed at night, and it will also fall by day.
There is no wall; he did not take hold of it. Who will appoint me to guard a reed in the field? Because of this warrior, I rejected him. For this reason, then, the Lord did everything he wished.
Those who live in it will cry out: I have burned! Let us make peace with him. Those who are coming, let us make peace.
Children of Jacob, give forth your blossoms, and Israel will blossom, and the inhabited world will be filled with its fruit.
Just as he himself struck, will they wound him in the same way? And just as he killed, will they kill him in the same way?
He will send them out, fighting and shaking them. Was it not you [?] meditating on the harsh word? He killed them with the spirit of his anger.

Therefore they will remove lawlessness from Jacob, and this is his blessing: when I remove his sin, when they make the stones of their altars into tiny pieces like crushed plaster, and their trees and their idols no longer remain, stripped bare like a woodland.
The enclosure fortified against the enemy will be abandoned like an enclosure that has been deserted. It will become a pasture for a long time, and they will rest there.

And after a time, nothing green will remain in it, because it has dried up. Come, women returning from a spectacle! For this is not a people with understanding. Therefore the one who made them will not have compassion on them, and the one who formed them will not show them mercy.
And on that day the Lord will cause turmoil from the channel of the river as far as Rhinocorura. But you, gather the children of Israel one by one.

And on that day the great trumpet will be sounded, and many peoples will come—those who were lost in the land of the Assyrians and those who were lost in Egypt. They will worship the Lord on the holy mountain of Zion in Jerusalem.
Woe to the crown of disgrace of Ephraim’s hired workers, the fading flower that has fallen from glory on the summit of the fertile mountain, those who are drunk without wine!

Look, the Lord’s anger is mighty and strong, like hail falling with no shelter beneath it, brought down violently; like abundant water sweeping through a country. He will give the land rest; he will do it by their hands
and their feet. And they will trample the crown of disgrace of Ephraim’s hired workers.
And the flower that has fallen from the hope of glory on the summit of the high mountain will be like an early fig: whoever sees it wants to swallow it before taking it in his hand.
On that day the Lord of hosts will become a crown of hope and glory, which he has woven for the remnant of the people.
And they will remain with a spirit of judgment, to administer justice, while he restrains the power to destroy.

For these are going astray through wine; they have gone astray because of strong drink. The priest and the prophet have staggered because of wine. They have been shaken by the stupor of strong drink and have gone astray—that is, a dream.
The curse will consume this plan, for this plan is for gain.
To whom have we announced bad news, and to whom have we announced a message? Those who have been weaned from their milk, those who have been taken away from the breast.
Expect affliction upon affliction: a little longer, a little longer. Expect hope upon hope: a little longer, a little longer.
Because of the disgrace of their lips, they will still speak to this people with a deceitful tongue,
those who say to it, “This is rest for the hungry, and this is destruction.” And they could not listen.

And the word of the Lord God will become for them affliction upon affliction and hope upon hope: a little longer, a little longer, so that they will go and many of them will fall backward. They will be endangered, shattered, and destroyed.
Therefore listen to the word of the Lord, you scoffing men and rulers of the people in Jerusalem,

because you said, “We have established a covenant with the underworld and an agreement with death. If a sweeping storm passes through us, it will not come upon us, because we have made falsehood our hope, and we will shelter ourselves in falsehood.”

Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Look, I will lay in the foundations of Zion a precious stone, a chosen cornerstone, honored in its foundations. Whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.
And I will make judgment a hope, and salvation, resting on my mercy, will become places to live. And you who trust vainly in falsehood, hoping that no storm will strike you,
lest your covenant with death be annulled—and your hope in the underworld will not endure—when the sweeping storm comes upon you, you will be trampled by it.
Whenever it passes through you, it will carry you away. The day will bring it morning after morning, and at night there will be an evil hope. Learn to listen!”
We who are hemmed in have no strength to fight, and we are too weak to gather together.
He will rise like the mountain of the ungodly and will be in the valley of Gibeon in anger. He will perform his deeds with bitter work. His anger will act in a strange way, and his goad is strange.
You too, do not rejoice, and do not let your bonds grow stronger, for we have heard of completed and decisive deeds from the Lord of hosts, which he will perform upon the whole earth.
Give ear and listen to my voice; pay attention and listen to my words.
Does the plowman plow all day, or prepare his seed before working the ground?
When he levels its surface, does he not then sow a little black cumin and cumin, and also sow wheat, barley, and spelt within a marked area?
You will be instructed by the judgment of their God, and you will rejoice.
For black cumin is not cleaned with a threshing sledge, nor does a cartwheel roll over cumin. Instead, black cumin is beaten out with a rod; but cumin—
they eat it with bread. I will not be angry with you forever, nor will the sound of my anger sweep you away.
These wonders came about through the Lord of hosts. Take counsel; lift up an empty consolation.
Woe to Ariel, the city that David fought against! Gather crops for yourselves. You will eat year after year; you will devour Moab.
For I will destroy Ariel, and her strength and her wealth will become mine.
I will encircle you like David, surround you with a rampart, and set up a tower against you.
Their words will be brought low to the ground, and their words will sink into the earth. Their voice will be like those who call out from the earth, and their voice will grow faint near the ground.
The wealth of the ungodly will become like dust from a wheel, and like chaff driven away. It will be like a moment, suddenly,
through the Lord of hosts. For there will be a visitation with shaking, thunder, and a great roaring noise, a sweeping wind, and a consuming flame of fire.

The wealth of all the nations will become like someone dreaming in his sleep—those who rose up against Israel, and everyone who rises up against Jerusalem, everyone who gathers against her and oppresses her.

They will be like hungry people who dream that they are eating, but when they wake up, their dream is empty; and like someone thirsty who drinks in a dream, but wakes up still thirsty, while his soul had trusted in something empty. This is how it will be with the wealth of all the nations that rose up against Jerusalem and against Mount Zion.
Become faint and bewildered, and become drunk, but not from strong drink or wine.
For the Lord has made you drink a spirit of anguish, and he will close their eyes, and those of their prophets and their rulers, who see [?] of hands.

All these words will become for you like the words of this sealed book. If it is given to someone who can read, with the instruction, “Read these,” he will say, “I cannot read them, for they are sealed.”
They will put the book into the hands of someone who cannot read, saying to him, “Read this.” And he will say, “I cannot read.”
The Lord said, “This people draws near to me; they honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments and teachings.”
Therefore, look, I will once again change this people, and I will change them. I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and hide the understanding of the intelligent.

Woe to those who make a secret plan that does not come from the Lord! Woe to those who make a deceitful plan! Their deeds will be in darkness, and they will say, “Who has seen us, and who will know us and the things we are doing?”

Are you not like the potter’s clay? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it, “You are not the one who shaped me”? Or will the thing made say to the one who made it, “You did not make me with understanding”?
Is it not just a little while before they transform Lebanon to be like Mount Carmel, and count Mount Carmel as a forest?
On that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind who are in darkness and gloom will see.
The poor will rejoice joyfully because of the Lord, and those who have no hope among people will be filled with joy.
The lawless person has failed, the proud person has perished, and those who act lawlessly in wickedness have been wiped out.
And those who make people sin through their words will lay a trap for anyone who rebukes them at the gates. They have turned the righteous person aside through acts of violence.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says concerning the house of Jacob, whom he set apart from Abraham: Jacob will no longer be ashamed, nor will Israel’s face grow pale now.
But when their children see my works, they will honor my name as holy because of me. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy, and they will fear the God of Israel.
Those who go astray in their spirit will gain understanding. Those who grumble will learn to listen, and stammering tongues will learn to speak peacefully.
Woe to the rebellious children! This is what the Lord says: You made a plan, but not through me, and agreements, but not through my Spirit, adding sin to your sins.
They travel down to Egypt, but they have not asked me to help them through Pharaoh or to shelter them through the Egyptians.
For Pharaoh’s shadow will become a shame to you and a disgrace to those who put their trust in Egypt.
For wicked leaders are in Tanis as messengers.
