For they will suffer in vain for a people who will not benefit them by helping them, but will bring shame and disgrace.

A vision concerning the animals in the wilderness: Amid distress and hardship, a lion and a lion cub come from that place, along with snakes and the flying offspring of snakes. They have brought their wealth on donkeys and camels to a nation that will not benefit them by helping them, but will bring shame and disgrace.
The Egyptians will give you reproaches and worthless things. Tell them, “This comfort of yours is worthless.”
Now, therefore, sit down and write these things on a tablet and in a book, for these things will remain for days and times and forever.
For this is a disobedient people, lying children who did not want to listen to the law of God.
They say to the prophets, “Do not instruct us,” and to those who see visions, “Do not speak to us. Instead, speak to us and tell us other deceptions.
Turn us away from the road and remove this path from us. Take the word of Israel away from us.”
Therefore, this is what the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says: You have refused to believe these words, and you have put your trust in falsehood, because you grumbled and came to trust in this word.
Therefore, this sin will be for you like a wall that has suddenly fallen, belonging to a lofty city that has been captured. Its fall comes suddenly.
Its fall will be like the shattering of a potter’s clay vessel into tiny pieces, so that no potsherd can be found among them to carry fire in or to draw a little water with.

This is what the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says: When you lie down and sigh, then you will be saved, and you will understand where you were in the days when you trusted in worthless things. Your strength became useless, and you did not want to listen.
Instead, you said, “We will flee on horses.” Therefore, you will flee. And you said, “We will ride swift mounts.” Therefore, those who pursue you will be swift.
A thousand will flee at the voice of one, and many will flee at the voice of five, until you become like a pole on a mountain and like a [?] carrying a banner on a hill.

And God will again wait to have compassion on you. Therefore, he will rise up to have mercy on you, for the Lord our God is a judge. Where will you leave your glory? Blessed are those who wait for him.
For a holy people will live in Zion. Jerusalem wept bitterly, for he will surely have mercy at the sound of her cry. When he saw, he listened to you.
And the Lord will give you bread of affliction and troubled water. Those who lead you astray will no longer approach you, for your eyes will see those who lead you astray.

Your ears will not listen to the words of those who lead you astray, or to the words of those who led you astray in the past, who said, “This is the road; let us walk along it,” whether to the right or to the left.

You will also defile the idols covered with silver and those covered with gold. You will break them into tiny pieces and scatter them like a woman's menstrual discharge, and sweep them away like dung.
Then rain will come for the seed in your land, and the bread from the seed in your land will be abundant and rich. On that day your cattle will graze in a lush, spacious place.
Your calves and cows that work the land will eat fodder mixed with clean barley.
On that day there will be flowing water on every high mountain and every lofty hill, when many perish and the tower falls.

The light of the moon will become like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times as bright, on that day when he heals the brokenness of his people and heals the pain of your wound.
Look, the name of the Lord is coming after a long time. The utterance of his lips is burning anger and glory. His utterance is full of wrath, and the wrath of his anger will consume like fire.

His breath comes like water flowing through a valley down to the ground. He will divide, throwing the nations into confusion because of their empty delusion. A delusion will pursue them and lead them onward.

Should you not rejoice at all times and enter the holy places at all times, like those who celebrate a festival and rejoice, entering with a flute to the mountain of God, into the presence of the mighty God, the Holy One of Israel?

And God will make them hear the glory of his voice. He will reveal the anger of his arm and strike them violently, with furious anger and a consuming flame of wrath, and like water and hail coming down together with violence.
For at the voice of the Lord, the Assyrians will be struck down by the blow with which he will strike them.
They will be around him, at the place where his hope of help lies, the help in which he trusted—those who were going to fight against him with their lyres and drums, by turns.
For they will slaughter you before the days. Have they also prepared for you to reign? A deep valley, cedar wood, fire, and much wood—the Lord's anger is like a valley set ablaze by sulfur.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who put their trust in horses and chariots, for they are numerous, and in the horses, which are exceedingly many. They did not believe in the Holy One of Israel and did not seek God.
He too is wise. He has brought disasters upon them, and they will not set aside his word. He will rise against the houses of wicked people and against their empty hope.
An Egyptian is a human being, not a god. Horses are flesh, not sources of help. But the Lord will bring his hand down upon them, and those who help them will suffer. They will all perish together.

For this is what the Lord said to me: “Just as a lion or a young lion roars over the prey it is about to seize, and keeps roaring over it until the mountains are filled with the sound of its anger and are shaken by its mounting anger, so the Lord of hosts will come down to lay waste to Mount Zion and its mountains.”
Like birds in flight, so the Lord will protect Jerusalem. He will rescue it, preserve it, and keep it alive.
And you who devise secret and lawless counsel.
For on that day people will remove from themselves their handmade idols of silver and gold, which their fingers made.
Assyria will fall by a sword that is not human, and a sword that is not human will devour him. He will not flee from a sword, and the young men will be struck down.

For they will trap them in a rock like a worm and strike them down. The one who flees will be caught. These are the things the Lord says: “Blessed is the one who has descendants in Zion and members of his household in Jerusalem.”
Look, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will rule with justice.
And it will happen that the man who hides his words will hide like someone swept along by water. He will appear in Zion like a flowing river, glorious in a thirsty land.
And they will no longer trust in a human being, but they will turn their ears to listen.
The hearts of the weak will pay attention and listen, and stammering tongues will quickly learn to speak peacefully.
They will no longer turn to say to the fool, “Be a ruler,” and from now on no servant will say, “Be silent.”
For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think about empty things, to carry out lawless deeds and speak falsely against the Lord, to scatter hungry souls and empty thirsty souls.
For the counsel of the wicked plans lawless deeds, to destroy the humble with unjust words and overturn the words of the humble in court.
But those who love God think about wise things, and this is the counsel that will endure.
Rise, wealthy women, and listen to my voice. Confident daughters, listen to my words.
Remember the days of the year with sorrow and hope. The harvest has ended; the sowing season has passed, and it will not come again soon.
Be dismayed and grieve, you who are confident. Strip yourselves bare and remain naked; tie sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for the desirable field and the fruit of the vine.
The land of my people will produce thorns and grass, and they will take joy away from Jerusalem, the wealthy city.

The houses are abandoned. They will leave the wealth of the cities. The fine houses of the villages will be deserted forever, a delight for the donkeys of the mountains and a grazing place for the shepherds.
Until a spirit comes upon you from on high, and Carmel becomes a wilderness, and Carmel is considered a woodland.
And justice will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel.
And the works of righteousness will be in peace, and righteousness will hold fast to rest and to those who believe forever.
And his people will live in hope forever, and his people will live in a peaceful city. He will dwell in security, and they will rest in prosperity.
But if hail falls, it will not fall on you, and those who live in the fields will be secure like those who live in the plain.
Blessed are those who sow beside every body of water, where the ox and the donkey tread.

Woe to those who afflict you, though no one will afflict you, and to the one who acts faithlessly but does not act faithlessly toward you. For those who act faithlessly will be destroyed, and they will be handed over. Like a moth in a garment, so they will be cut off.
Lord, have mercy on us, for we have trusted in you. Let the offspring of the unbelievers be destroyed, but let our salvation come in their time of distress.
At the sound of your terror, the peoples dispersed; at your terror, the nations scattered.
Now your plunder will be gathered, that of the small and the great. As someone gathers locusts, so they will mock you.
God is holy and dwells in the heights; Zion is filled with justice and righteousness.
They will be placed under the law, while our salvation is in treasures. Wisdom, understanding, and devotion to God come before the Lord: these are the treasures of righteousness.
Look, they will be afraid with the fear you felt. Those whom you fear will cry out, begging you for peace, for they will send messengers weeping bitterly and begging for peace.
For their roads will become deserted. The fear of the nations has ceased, and they will take away the righteousness that is among them, and they will not consider them human beings.
The earth mourned; Lebanon was put to shame; Sharon became a marsh. Galilee and Carmel will be laid bare.
“Now I will arise,” says the Lord. “Now I will be glorified; now I will be exalted.”
Now you will see; now you will be put to shame. The strength of your spirit will become empty; fire will consume you.
And the nations will burn like a thorn bush thrown into a field and set on fire.
Those who are far away will hear what I have done, and those who are near will know my power.
The lawless in Zion have stopped; trembling will seize the ungodly. Who will tell you that a fire will blaze? Who will tell you about the place of everlasting burning?

The one who walks in righteousness, who speaks of the straight path, who hates lawlessness and oppression, who shakes his hands free of bribes, who stops his ears so that he does not hear an unjust judgment, and who shuts his eyes so that he does not see oppression—
this is the one who will live in the high dwelling place of the solid rock. He will be given bread, and his water will be reliable.
You will see a king in glory, and your eyes will see a distant land.
Your soul will ponder the fear of the Lord. Where are your scribes? Where are your advisers? Where is the one who counts the stars?
Small and great—no one advised this one, nor did he know the deep voices, so that he did not hear. A despised people, and the one who hears has no understanding.

Look, the city of Zion! Your eyes will see salvation: Jerusalem, the city of the rich. Your tents will not be moved, nor will the stakes of your tents ever be moved, nor will your ropes be torn apart.

For the name of the Lord is great among you. There will be a place for you where the rivers and streams will be broad and spacious. You will not go along that route, nor will a ship travel there under sail.
For my God is great, and he will not pass by. The Lord is our father; the Lord is our judge; the Lord is our ruler; the Lord is our king. The Lord himself will save us.

Your ropes have broken because your mast was not strong, and it leaned over. Your sail will not be spread out, nor will it raise a signal until it is handed over as plunder. Now many lame people will take plunder.
And they will not say, “We are weary.” Nor will the people who live in it say this, for their sin has been forgiven.
Come near to me, nations, and listen, rulers. Let the earth listen, along with those who live in it, the inhabited world and its people.
For the Lord’s anger is coming upon all the nations, and his wrath upon their heads, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their shadows and their slain will lie cast out, their stench will rise, and the mountains will be drenched with their blood.
The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves dropping from a grapevine and like leaves falling from a fig tree.
My sword has become drunk in heaven. Look, it is coming down upon Idumea and upon the people doomed to destruction, in judgment.
The Lord’s sword is drenched in blood; it has grown fat from the fat of lambs and the fat of goats and rams. For the Lord’s sacrifice is in Bozrah, and there is a great slaughter in Edom.
And the mighty will fall with them, along with the rams and calves. The earth will become drunk with their blood and will be filled with their fat.
For the Lord’s day of judgment and the year of repayment for Zion have drawn near upon them.
And its streams will turn into pitch, and its soil into sulfur, and its land will burn like pitch.
Night and day it will never be extinguished, and its smoke will rise to heaven. It will remain desolate for generations, for a long time.
And birds will live in it, along with hedgehogs, ibises, and ravens. They will stretch a measuring line of desolation over it, and donkey-centaurs will live in it.
Its rulers will be no more, for its kings and its rulers will be destroyed.
And thorn bushes will grow in its cities and its high places. It will become a dwelling for sirens and an enclosure for ostriches.
And demons will meet donkey-centaurs, and they will cry out to one another. The donkey-centaurs will rest there, for they have found a resting place for themselves.
There the hedgehog raised her young, and the earth kept her young safe. There the deer met and saw one another’s faces.
They came out in full number. Not one of them was lost, and not one had to look for another, because the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them.
He cast lots for them, and his hand divided the pastureland among them. You will inherit it forever, generation after generation, and they will rest on it.
Rejoice, thirsty wilderness! Let the wilderness rejoice and blossom like a lily.
The deserts of the Jordan will blossom and rejoice. The glory of Lebanon and the splendor of Carmel have been given to it. My people will see the glory of the Lord and the majesty of God.
Strengthen the weak hands and the unsteady knees.
Encourage those who are fainthearted: Do not be afraid! Look, our God will repay with judgment, and he will repay them. He is the one who is coming to save us.
Then the eyes of the blind will open, and the ears of the deaf will hear.
Then the lame will leap like deer, and the tongue of those unable to speak will become clear, because water has flowed in the desert, and a stream in thirsty land.
The place without water will become a marsh, and there will be a spring of water in thirsty land. Birds will rejoice there, and reeds and marshes will be there in the cattle pens.

They will call it the pure and holy road. No unclean person will pass through that place, nor will there be an unclean road there. But those who have been scattered will walk on it, and they will not go astray.
No lion will be there, nor will any dangerous wild animal go up onto it, nor will any be found there. Instead, those who have been redeemed will walk on it.

Gathered together, they will return because of the Lord and come to Zion with joy. Everlasting joy will be upon their heads, for blessing will be upon them. Joy and gladness will overtake them; sorrow, heartache, and sighing have fled.
And in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came up against the fortified cities of Judea and captured them.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army. He stood at the channel of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace steward, came out to him, along with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: In whom do you put your trust?
Can a battle be fought with counsel and advice spoken by lips? Now, then, in whom have you put your trust, so that you do not obey me?
Look, you are relying on that broken reed staff, Egypt. If someone leans on it, it will pierce his hand. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to everyone who trusts in him.
If you say, ‘We have put our trust in the Lord our God’—
Now make a wager with our lord, the king of Assyria, and I will give you a thousand horses, if you can provide riders for them.
How will you be able to look the governors in the face? Those who put their trust in the Egyptians for a horse and a rider are servants.
Now, then, have I come up against this country to fight it without the Lord? The Lord is the one who told me, ‘Go and destroy it.’”

Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace steward, and Shebna the secretary said to him, “Speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?”

Rabshakeh said to them, “Did my lord send me to your lord or to you? Did he not send me to the people on the wall, so that they may eat their own excrement and drink their own urine together with you?”
Rabshakeh stood up and called out in a loud voice in Hebrew, “Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king of Assyria says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words that have no power to save you.
And do not let Hezekiah tell you, “God will rescue you, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”

Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: “If you want to receive a blessing, come out to me. Then each of you may eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and you may drink water from your own well,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and wine, bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah deceive you by saying, ‘God will rescue you.’ Has any of the gods of the nations rescued his country from the king of Assyria?
Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? And where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim? Were they able to rescue them, or to rescue Samaria from my hand?
Which of all the gods of the nations has rescued his land from my hand, that God should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?”
They remained silent, and no one answered him a word, because the king had ordered that no one should answer.
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, Shebna, the army’s secretary, and Ahaz son of Asaph, the recorder, went in to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him what the Rabshakeh had said.
When Hezekiah heard the Rabshakeh’s words, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went up to the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim the steward, Shebna the secretary, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

They said to him, “This is what Hezekiah says: ‘Today is a day of distress, insult, reproach, and wrath, because the woman in labor has reached the point of giving birth, but she has no strength to give birth.

May the Lord your God hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria sent to insult the living God, and to insult him with these words that the Lord your God has heard. And pray to the Lord your God for those who remain.’”
And the king’s servants came to Isaiah.

And Isaiah said to them, “This is what you are to say to your master: ‘This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of the Assyrians have insulted me.’”
“Look, I will send a spirit upon him, and he will hear a report and return to his own country. He will fall by the sword in his own land.”
The Rabshakeh returned and found the king besieging Libnah.
The king of Assyria heard that Asaratha, king of the Cushites, had come out to besiege him. When he heard this, he turned back and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
This is what you are to say to Hezekiah, king of Judea: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say, ‘Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of the Assyrians.’”
“Or have you not heard what the kings of Assyria have done to the whole land, how they destroyed it?
Did the gods of the nations rescue those whom my ancestors destroyed—Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, those in the region of Teman?
Where are the kings of Hamath? Where is Arpad? And where are Hena and Ivvah, belonging to the city of Sepharvaim?”
And Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and opened the letter before the Lord.
And Hezekiah prayed to God, saying:
Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who sits enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God and Lord of all the kingdoms of the inhabited world. You made heaven and earth.
“Listen, Lord! Look, Lord, and see the words that Sennacherib, king of Assyria, has sent to insult the living God.
For the kings of Assyria have indeed laid waste the whole inhabited world and their territory.
They threw their idols into the fire, because they were not gods but things made by human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
Now, therefore, Lord our God, save us from their hands, so that every kingdom on earth may know that you alone are God.”

And Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah, and he said to him, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘I have heard the prayers you offered to me concerning Sennacherib, king of Assyria.’”
This is the word that the Lord spoke about him: “He despised and mocked the virgin daughter of Zion, and he shook his head at you, daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom have you insulted, and whom have you mocked? Whom have you blasphemed, or against whom have you raised your hand? Yet you did not lift your eyes to the Holy One of Israel.

For you insulted the Lord through messengers. You said, ‘With my many chariots I climbed to the heights of the mountains and the slopes of Lebanon. I cut down its tall cedars and its beautiful cypresses, and I entered the lofty beauty of its forest.
I established rivers; I turned water into a desert, along with every gathering of water.’
Are these not the things you heard long ago, which I did from ancient days and determined? But now I have set about laying waste strong nations in fortified places, who live in lofty cities.
They gave up and withered, becoming like dry grass on rooftops and like weeds.
But now I know your resting, your going out, and your coming in.
The anger with which you raged, and your arrogance, have reached me. I will put a hook in your nose and a bridle between your lips, and turn you back along the road by which you came.
This will be a sign for you: eat this year what you have sown, and in the second year what remains. But in the third year you will sow and reap, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
Those who remain in the land of Judah will put down roots and bear fruit above.
For there will be survivors in Jerusalem, and those who escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord will do these things.
Therefore this is what the Lord says about the king of the Assyrians: He will not enter this city, nor shoot an arrow at it, nor bring a shield against it, nor build a siege ramp against it.
Instead, he will return along the road by which he came. These are the things the Lord says:
I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”
The angel of the Lord went out and killed 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When they rose in the morning, they found all the bodies dead.
Then the king of the Assyrians turned back and departed, and he settled in Nineveh.
While he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch, his ancestral god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with swords. They fled to Armenia, and his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.

At that time Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Put your household in order, for you will die and will not live.”
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,
saying, “Remember, Lord, how I walked before you in faithfulness and with a sincere heart, and did what pleases you in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
The word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:
“Go and tell Hezekiah: This is what the Lord, the God of David your father, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life.
I have rescued you from the king of the Assyrians, and I will defend this city.
This will be a sign for you from the Lord that God will fulfill this word:

Look, I will turn back the shadow on your steps, on which the sun has gone down—the steps of your father’s house. I will turn the sun back ten steps.” And the sun went up over the ten steps on which the shadow had gone down.
The prayer of Hezekiah, king of Judea, when he became ill and recovered from his illness.
I said in the prime of my days, “I will leave the rest of my years at the gates of the underworld.”
I said, “I will no longer see God's salvation on the earth. I will no longer see people

from my family.” I left behind the remainder of my life. My spirit came out of me and departed like someone who has finished pitching a tent. My life became to me like cloth on a loom, ready to be cut off.
On that day, if I was handed over until morning to a lion, it crushed my bones in this way, for I was handed over from day until night.
I will cry out like a swallow, and I will murmur like a dove. For my eyes grew weary as I looked toward the height of heaven, toward the Lord, who rescued me and removed
the anguish of my soul.
For you were told about it, Lord, and you revived my breath. When you comforted me, you brought me back to life.
For you saved my soul from destruction, and my life, and you turned all my sins back behind me.
Those in the underworld will not praise you, and those who have died will not bless you. Nor will those in the underworld hope for your mercy.
The living will bless you as I do. For from today onward I will have children who will tell of your mercy.
The Lord of my salvation! I will not stop blessing you with a harp all the days of my life, before the house of God.
And Isaiah the prophet said to Hezekiah, “Take a cake of figs, crush it, and smear yourself with it, and you will recover.”
And Hezekiah said, “This is the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord God.”
At that time Merodach, son of Baladan, king of Babylonia, sent letters, greetings, and gifts to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been sick to the point of death and had recovered.

Hezekiah rejoiced greatly over them, and he showed them the treasury, the myrrh, the incense, the ointment, the silver, the gold, all the rooms containing his valuable possessions, and everything in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house that Hezekiah did not show them.

And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What are these men saying, and where have they come from to visit you?” And Hezekiah said, “They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.”

And Isaiah said, “What did they see in your house?” And Hezekiah said, “They saw everything in my house, and there is nothing in my house that they did not see, as well as the other things in my storehouses.”
And Isaiah said, “Listen to the word of the Lord of hosts:

Look, days are coming when they will take everything in your house, together with everything your ancestors have gathered until this day, and carry it to Babylon. They will leave nothing behind. God has said this.
‘They will take some of your sons whom you have fathered and make them eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.’”
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word that the Lord has spoken is good. Let there be peace and righteousness in my days.”
God said, “Comfort, comfort my people.
Priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem. Comfort her, for her humiliation has grown and her sin has been forgiven, because she has received from the Lord's hand double for her sins.”
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: “Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be lowered. All the crooked places will become straight, and the rough places will become smooth roads.”
And the glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see the glory of God.
The voice of someone saying, “Cry out!” And I said, “What should I cry out?” “All flesh is grass, and all human glory is like a flower of grass.”
The grass has dried up, and its flower has fallen.
But the word of the Lord remains forever.

Go up onto a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion. Raise your voice with strength, you who proclaim good news to Jerusalem. Raise it; do not be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is our God!”
Here is the Lord, coming with power, and his arm comes with authority. His reward is with him, and his work is before him.
He will tend his flock like a shepherd, and he will gather his lambs into his arm, and he will comfort those that are pregnant.
Who measured the water in the palm of his hand, the sky with his handspan, and the whole earth with his handful? Who measured the mountains with a measure and the hills with a balance?
Who understood the mind of the Lord, and who became his adviser to enlighten him?
Or with whom did he take counsel, who instructed him? Or who taught him judgment, or showed him the way of wisdom? Or who first gave him anything, so that he would repay him?
If all the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are counted like the tilt of a balance, and have been compared to spit,
yet Lebanon is not enough for burning, and all its animals are not enough for an offering.
And all the nations are nothing, and they have been counted as nothing.
To whom have you compared the Lord, and to what kind of thing have you likened him?
To an image that a carpenter made? Or was it a goldsmith who melted gold and overlaid it, or fashioned it into a form?
For the carpenter carves wood that does not rot, and skillfully seeks to set up an image so that it will not move.
Do you not know? Do you not hear? Were you not told from the beginning? Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?
He who holds the circle of the earth, whose inhabitants are like locusts, is the one who established the sky like a vault and spread it out like a tent to live in.
He makes rulers rule over nothing, and makes the earth like nothing.
For they will not be sown or planted, nor will their root take root in the earth. A wind blew on them, and they dried up, and the whirlwind will carry them away like stalks.
Now then, to whom have you compared me, and I will be exalted?” says the Holy One.

Lift your eyes to the sky and see who created all these things. He brings out their array according to their number; he will call them all by name. With great glory and powerful might, you forget none.
Do not say, Jacob—and what is it that you have said, Israel?—“My way is hidden from my God,” and, “God has taken away my judgment and turned it aside.”

Now, have you not understood, although you have heard? The everlasting God is the one who created the ends of the earth. He does not grow hungry, nor will he grow weary, and there is no way to understand his wisdom.
He who gives strength to the hungry and sorrow to those who are not distressed.
For little children will grow hungry, young men will grow weary, and the chosen will lose their strength.
But those who wait for God will renew their strength. They will grow wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not grow hungry.
Be renewed before me, islands, for the rulers will change their strength. Let them come forward and speak together; then let them pronounce judgment.

Who raised up righteousness from the east? He called her, and she followed him. He will place her before the nations and make kings marvel. He will lay their swords on the ground and make their bows like scattered stubble.
And he will pursue them, for the path of his feet will proceed in peace.
Who acted and did these things and called her? It is he who calls her from the first generations. I am God from the beginning, and afterward I am still the same.
The nations saw and were afraid. The ends of the earth drew near and came together.
Each one judges his neighbor, and each one helps his brother, and he will say:
A carpenter grew strong, and a metalworker strikes the anvil while smoothing it. At one point he says, “It is a good joint.” He secured them with nails; they will be fixed in place and will not move.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, whom I loved.
The one whom I took to myself from the end of the earth—and I called you from its hidden places—I said to you, “You are my servant.” I chose you and did not abandon you.

Do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not go astray, and I will be glorified in you. I myself said, “I have labored in vain for empty things.” Do not go astray, for I am God, who gave you strength. I helped you and upheld you with my righteous right hand.
Look, everyone who opposes you will be ashamed and disgraced. They will become like those who do not exist, and all your enemies will perish.
You will search for them and will not find anyone who rises against you, for they will become like those who do not exist, and those who oppose you will cease to exist.
For I am God, who holds your right hand, who says to you, “Do not be afraid.”
Jacob, weak Israel, I am the one who helped you, says God, who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I have made you like the wheels of a new threshing cart with sawlike teeth that thresh. You will thresh the mountains and crush the hills, making them like chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and a whirlwind will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

Let the poor rejoice along with the needy, for they will seek water and find none. Their tongues have dried up from thirst. I am the Lord God; I am the one who will hear, the Lord God of Israel, and I will not abandon them.
Instead, I will open rivers on the mountains and springs among the rocks. I will turn the wilderness into a marsh and the thirsty land into springs.
I will put cedars in the thirsty land, along with boxwood, myrtle, cypress, and pine.
So that they may see and understand, reflect and know together that the Lord’s hand made all these things, and that the Holy One of Israel revealed them.
Your case has come near, says the Lord God. Your plans have come forward, says the King of Jacob.
Let them come forward and tell us what will happen. Or say what the first things are, so that we may set our minds on them and understand what the last things are.
And tell us the things that are coming afterward, so that we may understand that you are gods. Do good, and let us do evil, so that we may marvel and see together.
For where are you from, and where does your work come from? They chose you as an abomination from the earth.

But I raised up one from the north and one from where the sun rises. They will be called by my name. Let the rulers come. And like a potter’s clay, and as a potter treads his clay, that is how you will be trampled.

For who tells of things from the beginning so that we might understand, and of earlier things so that we may say, “They are true”? There is no one who tells of things before they happen, nor anyone who hears your words.
I will give Zion a beginning, and I will encourage Jerusalem on the way.
For look, there is no one among the nations, and there is no one among their idols who can tell anything. If I ask them, “Where are you from?” they will not answer me.
For your makers exist, and those who mislead you are worthless.
Jacob, my son, I will accept him as mine. Israel, my chosen one, my soul has accepted him. I have put my Spirit upon you. He will bring forth justice to the nations.
He will not cry out or shout, and his voice will not be heard outside.
He will not break a bruised reed, and he will not extinguish a smoldering flax wick. Instead, he will bring forth his justice in truth.
He will shine and will not be crushed until he establishes justice on the earth. The nations will trust in his name.

This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says—the one who created heaven and established it, who established the earth and everything in it, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I am the Lord God, who called you in righteousness. I will take hold of your hand and give you strength. I have appointed you as a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring those who are bound out of their bonds, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
I am the Lord God. This is my name. I will not give my glory to another, or my praise to things made by human hands.
Look, the former things have come to pass. I myself will announce new things, and before I send them, I have told you about them.
Praise God with a new [?]. All his dominion, glorify his name from the ends of the earth—you who go down to the sea and sail upon it, the islands and those who live in them.
Rejoice, wilderness and its villages, the settlements and those who live in Kedar. Those who live among the rocks will rejoice and shout from the mountain peaks.
They will give glory to God and proclaim his praises in the islands.
The Lord God of hosts is coming forth. He will crush war, stir up zeal, and shout against his enemies with power.
I have been silent. Will I remain silent forever and endure? I have borne it like a woman about to give birth. I will tear them apart and dry them up all at once.
I will turn the rivers into islands and dry up the marshes.

I will lead the blind out along a road they have not known, and I will make them walk on paths they do not know. I will turn darkness into light for them and make crooked places straight. These are the things I will do for them, and I will not abandon them.
But they have turned back. Be utterly ashamed, you who trust in things made by human hands, who say to cast images, “You are our gods.”
Listen, you deaf people! Lift up your eyes, you blind people, so that you may see.
And who are blind except my servants, and deaf except those who rule over them? And the servants of God have become blind.
You have seen many times but have not paid attention. Your ears are open, but you have not listened.
The Lord God decided that he would give honor and exalt a blessing. And I saw.

Look, the people have been robbed and plundered. For the trap is in the storerooms everywhere, and in the houses as well, in the place where they hid them. They have become plunder, with no one to rescue them; spoil, with no one saying, “Release them!”
Who among you will listen to these things? Listen to what is coming.
Who gave Jacob over to plunder, and Israel to those who rob him? Was it not God, against whom he sinned? They did not want to walk in his ways or listen to his law.
And he brought the fury of his anger down upon them, but war overpowered them, and those who burned them were all around them. Yet not one of them understood, nor did they take these things to heart.
Now this is what the Lord God says, the one who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, because I have chosen you. I have called you by my name; you are mine.
Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and the rivers will not drown you. If you pass through fire, you will not be burned, and no flame will scorch you.
For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, who saves you. Look, I have given Egypt in exchange for you, and Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
Since you became precious in my sight, you have been honored, and I have loved you. I will give many people in your place, and rulers in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bring your descendants from the east, and I will gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, “Bring them,” and to the west, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from the distant land and my daughters from the end of the earth.”
Everyone who has been called by my name—for I created him for my glory, and I formed him and made him.
I brought out a blind people, and those who have eyes are also blind, and their ears are closed.

All the nations have gathered together, and the rulers among them will assemble. Who will declare these things? Or who will tell you what happened in the beginning? Let them bring their witnesses and be justified, and let [?].

Be witnesses for me, and I am the witness, says God, along with my son whom I have chosen, so that you may know, understand, and believe that I am God. No other god came into being before me, and there is none after me.
I am the Lord God, and there is no other besides me who saves.
I told you, and I saved you; I reproved you, and there was nothing foreign among you. You are my witnesses, and I am the witness, says the Lord God.
Even from the beginning, and there is no one who can escape from my hands. I will act, and who will turn me back?
This is what the Lord God says, the one who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I will send to Babylon and raise up all those who flee, and they will bind the Chaldeans in ships.
I am the Lord, your holy God, who made Israel king over you.
This is what the Lord God says, the one who gave you a road through the sea and a path through abundant water,
who brought out chariots and horses and a great multitude. But they lay down and will not rise. They were extinguished, like a wick that has been extinguished.
Do not remember the ancient things, and do not consider the former things.
Look, I will do new things. These will now appear, and you will recognize them. I will make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the place where there is no water.

The wild animals of the countryside will praise me, the sirens and the young ostriches, because I have provided water in the wilderness and rivers in the place where there is no water, to give my people something to drink.
My chosen people, whom I brought into being to proclaim my virtues.
I have not called you now, Jacob, nor have I wearied you, Israel.
The sheep offered as your burnt offering were not for me, and you have not honored me with your sacrifices. Nor have you served me with your sacrifices, nor have I wearied you with incense.
Nor have you bought aromatic reed for me with money, nor have I desired the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, with your sins and your acts of injustice, you have burdened me.
I am the one, I am the one who wipes away your sins, and I will not remember them.
But you, remember, and let us go to judgment. Tell your lawless deeds first, so that you may be justified.
Your ancestors who came before you and your rulers acted lawlessly against me.
And your rulers profaned my holy things, and I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to ridicule.
But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the Lord God says, he who created you and formed you from the womb: “I have helped you. Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and Israel my beloved, whom I have chosen.
For I will give water to those who walk thirstily in a place where there is no water. I will put my Spirit upon your descendants and my blessings upon your children.
And they will spring up like grass amid water and like a willow tree beside flowing water.
One will say, ‘I belong to God,’ and another will call out the name of Jacob. Another will write, ‘I belong to God,’ and will cry out the name of Israel.
This is what God says, the king of Israel, who rescued you, the eternal God of hosts: “I am the first, and I am also the one who comes afterward, and there is no other god besides me.
Who is like me? Let him stand up, let him call out, and let him prepare things for me, from the time I created humanity and forever. Let them tell you what is coming before it comes.
Do not abandon [?]. From the beginning you heard, and I told you about these things. You are witnesses. Was there another god besides me? Those who fashion things did not exist,
and those who carve are all worthless—those who make things according to the thoughts of their hearts, things that will not benefit them. Instead, they will be put to shame,
all those who fashion gods and carve things that have no benefit in them.
And they all dried up in the place where they were made, and they do not listen to anyone. Let them all gather and stand up. Let them turn pale and be put to shame together.

For a craftsman sharpened his chisel. He worked on it with his [?] and set it upright with his hammer. He worked on it with his strong arm. He will grow hungry and become weak, and he will not drink water.

For a craftsman carved a piece of wood, set it upright according to a measurement, and fixed it with [?]. He made it in the shape of a human being, to stand it in a house, resembling the beauty of a human being.
This wood, which he cut down in the field, is what the Lord established, and the rain made it grow.
A person finds it to burn, and he takes some of it and warms himself. When he burns it, he bakes bread with it. They make the rest into gods and worship them.

They burned half of it in the fire, and when they burned it, they baked bread over it. He roasted meat over it, ate, and was satisfied. When he became warm, he said, ‘This is good! I have become warm, and I have seen the fire.’
He made the rest into a god, a handmade idol, and bowed down to it and prayed to it, saying, “Save me, because you are my god.”
They did not understand how to be wise, because they became blind, unable to see with their eyes or understand with their hearts.

And they did not reflect in their souls or understand in their hearts that they burned half of it in the fire and baked bread on its coals, and that he roasted meat and ate it, while he made the remainder into an abomination and worshiped it.
Understand that their heart is ashes, and it leads them astray. No one can save their souls. Look—you will not say, ‘What is in my right hand is a lie.’
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you to be my servant. You are mine. And you, Israel, do not forget me.
For look, I will wipe away your sins like a cloud and your lawless deeds like mist. Return to me, and I will redeem you.

Rejoice, heavens, for God has had mercy on Israel. Sound the trumpet, foundations of the earth. Mountains, cry out with joy, and you forests and all the trees upon them, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will receive glory.
This is what the Lord says, he who redeemed you and formed you from the womb: “I am the Lord, who accomplishes everything. I stretched out heaven by myself, and I made the earth firm.
Who is the other who has frustrated the signs of those who speak from within themselves and those who divine from their hearts, who turns the wise back and makes their counsel foolish,

who confirms the word of his son and makes the counsel of his messengers true, who says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be inhabited,’ and to the cities of Judea, ‘You will be built,’ and, ‘Her deserted places will spring up,’
who says to the deep, ‘You will become dry, and I will make your rivers dry up.’
The one who says, “Think of the Lord, and you will carry out all my wishes”; the one who says to Jerusalem, “They will rebuild you, and I will lay the foundation of my holy house.”

This is what the Lord God says to my anointed, Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped so that nations will obey him: “I will break the power of kings. I will open doors before him, and cities will not be shut.”
“I will go before him and level the mountains. I will smash the bronze doors and break the iron bars.”

“I will give you treasures of darkness in hidden places where they cannot be seen. I will open them for you so that you may know that I am the Lord your God, who calls you by name, the God of Israel.”
“For the sake of Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen one, I will call you by my name and take you for myself, although you did not know me.”
“For I am the Lord God, and there is no other god besides me, although you did not know me.”
So that those in the places where the sun rises and those in the places where it sets may know that there is none besides me.
“I am the one who prepared the light and made the darkness. I am the one who makes peace and creates evil. I am the Lord God, who makes all these things.”
Let heaven rejoice above, and let the clouds rain down righteousness. Let the earth bring forth mercy, and let it bring forth righteousness at the same time, for I am the Lord God who created you.

What more could I have done? I made you like a potter’s clay. Will the plowman drag the soil all day long? Will the clay say to the potter, “Why are you making me? You are not working,” or, “You have no hands”?
Or will the thing that was formed answer back to the one who formed it? Will someone say to his father, “Why are you fathering me?” or to his mother, “Why are you in labor?”
For this is what the Lord God says, the Holy One of Israel, who made the things that are to come: “Ask me about my sons and my daughters, and you give me orders about the works of my hands.”
“I made the earth and humanity upon it. With my hand I established heaven. I gave orders to all the stars.”

“I raised up the king in righteousness, and all his paths are straight. He is the one who will build my city, and he will bring back my captive people, not for ransom or for honors,” says the Lord of Hosts.

This is what the Lord of Hosts says: The labor of Egypt and the trade of the Ethiopians, and the Sabeans, tall men, are coming to you. They will become your servants and follow you, bound with bronze chains on their hands. They will bow down to you and pray to you, saying, “God is in you, and there is no other god besides you.”
For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior.
Look, all who oppose him will be ashamed and disgraced, and they will walk in shame. Renew yourselves before me, islands.
Israel will be saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation. They will never be ashamed or disgraced.

This is what the Lord says, the one who made heaven—he is God—the one who prepared the earth and made it. He is the one who spread it out. He did not make it for emptiness, but for people to live in it: “I am he, I am he, and there is no other besides me.”
“I did not speak in secret or in a dark place of the earth. I did not say to Jacob’s descendants, ‘Seek something worthless.’ I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and declares the truth.”

Gather together and come; take counsel together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those who carry a piece of wood made by their own hands, and those who pray to gods that cannot save them, have no understanding.

If they are going to answer, let them draw near so that they may understand together. Who made these things known from the beginning? When were they told to you? I am God, and there is no other besides me, righteous and a savior; there is no other apart from me.
Turn to me so that you may live, you who are at the ends of the earth, says the Lord. I am God, and there is no other.
“I will swear by myself: righteousness comes from my mouth, and my words will not turn back. Every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will swear by God,”
saying, “Righteousness and glory come to him.” And all those who separate themselves
from the Lord will be ashamed. All the descendants of the children of Israel will be justified and glorified in God.
Bel has fallen; Dagon has been smashed. Their handmade images have been put on wild beasts and livestock. Carry them bound like [?].
And they are hungry and exhausted, all of them powerless. These cannot save them in war, and they themselves have been carried away as captives.
Listen, house of Jacob and all the remnant of Israel, you who have been carried from the womb and taught from your infancy.

Until their old age, I am he, and until you grow old, I am still he. I am the one who sustains you. I am the one who made you, and I am also the one who will release you. I am the one who will take you to myself and rescue you.
To whom have you compared me? Look and think, you who go astray.
Those who buy gold from their purses and weigh silver on a balance by weight hired a goldsmith and made objects fashioned by hand. He bows down to it and worships it.

They lift them onto their shoulders and walk with them. But when they set them down, they remain in their place and do not move. They do not hear anyone who cries out to them, nor will they rescue him from troubles.
Remember these things and groan. Repent, you who have gone astray; turn back in your hearts.
Remember and understand the things of old, from eternity: I am God, and there is no other god besides me.
I announce the last things from the beginning, before they happen, and bring them to completion all at once. I said, “My entire plan will stand, and I will do everything I desire.”
The one who calls a bird from the east and from a distant land concerning the things I have planned. I spoke and brought him; I created him and made him. I brought him and made his path straight.
Listen to me, you whose hearts have gone astray, who are far from righteousness.
I have brought my righteousness near, together with my truth, and I will not delay my salvation, which comes from me. I have given salvation to Israel in Zion, for the glory of the Lord.
Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter of Babylon, daughter of the Chaldeans. They will no longer call you tender and delicate.
Take millstones for yourself and grind flour. Uncover your veil, uncover your gray hair, uncover your shins, and cross rivers.
Your shame will be exposed, and your disgrace will be revealed. I will exact justice from you; from now on I will not hand you over to people.
The one who rescues you—the Lord of Hosts is his name—is the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in grief; go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. From now on they will no longer call you the power of the kingdom.
I cast it upon my people, and it defiled my inheritance. I myself handed my inheritance over to you, but you showed them no mercy. You made the old man's yoke exceedingly heavy.
And you said, “I will be a ruler forever.” You did not consider these things in your heart, nor did you remember the last things.

Now, then, listen to these things, you who are called tender, who feel secure, who say in your heart, “I am, and there is no one else besides me. I will not sit as a widow, and I will not experience bereavement.”
But now these two things are coming upon you in a single day: widowhood and childlessness are coming upon you suddenly, through your sorcery and the great power of your enchanters.

In the hope of your wickedness. For you said, “I am, and there is no one else.” Understand that the wisdom of these things and your prostitution will bring you shame. And you said in your heart, “I am, and there is no one else.”

Destruction is coming upon you, and you will not recognize a pit, and you will fall into it. Misery is coming upon you, and you will not be able to cleanse yourself. Misery is coming upon you suddenly, without your knowing it.
Stand now with your enchantments and your sorcery, which you have learned since your childhood, so that you may be able to gain some benefit.
You have labored in counsel. Let those who calculate the times of the heavens stand up and save you. Let those who observe the stars tell you what is coming upon you.
For look, they will all burn like straw upon a fire, and they will not be able to save their lives from the flame, for you have coals of fire to sit upon.
This is what your help will be like. You have labored in your trade since your childhood. Each person has gone astray on his own, and no salvation will come to you.

Listen to these things, house of Jacob, you who were called by the name of Israel and came from Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, and remember him, but not in truth or righteousness.
And you who trust in the name of this holy city and rely on the God of Israel—the Lord of Hosts is his name.
I announced the former things beforehand. They came from my mouth, and people heard them. I did them suddenly, and they [?].
I know that you are stubborn: your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead is bronze.

I told you about these things beforehand, before they came upon you. You heard them. Do not say, “The idols did these things for me,” and do not say, “The images fashioned by hand [?] and the cast images commanded these things for me.”
You heard all these things, yet you did not understand. But I also told you about the new things that will happen from now on, and you did not speak of them.
For they will happen now, and not previously. You did not hear them in earlier days. Do not say, “Yes, I know them.”
You neither understood them nor knew them, nor did you open your ears from the beginning. For I knew that you would act treacherously, and that you would be called lawless from the womb.
For the sake of my name, I will keep you safe from my anger, and I will bring my glorious deeds upon you, so that I will not wipe you out.
Look, I did not sell you for money, but I rescued you from the furnace of poverty.
I will do these things for you for my own sake, because my name is being reviled, and I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I call. I am the first, and I am the last forever.
My hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand made the sky firm. I will call them all, and they will stand together.
They will all gather together and listen. Who will tell them such things? Know yourself [?]. I carried out your will against Babylon, to remove the descendants of the Chaldeans.
I spoke; I called him; I brought him, and I made his path straight.

Come near me and listen to these things. From the beginning, I did not say them in secret, nor in a place in the dark earth. I was there when they were about to happen. Now the Lord has sent me, and his Spirit.
This is what your rescuer, the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I am your God. I taught you to find the path on which you should walk.”
If you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been like the sand, and the children born from you like the dust of the earth. Even now, I will not wipe you out, nor will your name perish from my presence.
Come out of Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Speak with a joyful voice, and let them hear this. Proclaim it to the end of the earth. Say, “The Lord has rescued his servant Jacob.”
And if they become thirsty in the wilderness, he will bring them water, and he will bring it out of the rock for them. A rock will split, water will flow out, and the people will drink.
“There is no joy for the ungodly,” says the Lord.
Listen to me, islands, and pay attention, nations. They will come into being after a long time, says the Lord. He called me by my name while I was inside my mother.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me beneath the shadow of his hand. He made me like a chosen arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, and I will be glorified through you.”
But I said, “I have labored in vain, for nothing, and spent my strength for no purpose. Therefore my judgment is with [?] the Lord, and my labor is before my God.”

Now this is what the Lord says, who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to gather Jacob and Israel to him: “They will gather me to him, and I will be honored before the Lord, and God will be my strength.”

And he said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called my servant, to establish the tribes of Jacob for me and to bring back the scattered people of Israel. Look, I have made you a covenant for a people, a light for the nations, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.”

This is what the Lord who rescued you, the God of Israel, says: “Purify the one who despises his own soul, the one detested by the nations, a servant of rulers. Kings will see him, and rulers will rise and bow down to him because of the Lord, because the Holy One of Israel is faithful, and I have chosen you.”

This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “I listened to you at an acceptable time, and I helped you on a day of salvation. I gave you as a covenant for the nations, to establish the earth and to inherit the inheritance of the wilderness.”
Saying to those in chains, “Come out,” and to those in darkness, “Show yourselves.” They will be pastured along all their roads, and their pasture will be in every place where people walk.
They will not hunger or thirst, nor will the scorching heat or the sun strike them. Instead, the one who has mercy on them will comfort them and lead them out beside springs of water.
I will make every mountain into a road, and every path into a pasture for them.
Look, these are coming from far away, and these others from the north and the sea, and still others from the land of the Persians.
Rejoice, heavens, and let the earth celebrate! Let the mountains cry out with joy and leap with righteousness, because God has had mercy on his people and has comforted the humble among his people.
But Zion said, “God has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
“Will a mother forget her children and have no mercy on those born from her womb? Even if a woman forgets them, I will not forget them, Jerusalem,” says the Lord.
“Look, I have drawn your walls on my hands, and you are always before me.
They will quickly be rebuilt by those who destroyed them, and those who laid you waste are leaving you.
Lift your eyes all around and see all your children. Look, they have gathered together and come to you. As I live,” says the Lord, “you will put them all on and wear them like a bride’s adornment.
For your deserted places, your ruined places, and those that have fallen will now be too cramped for their inhabitants, and those who devour you will be far from you.
For the children you lost will say in your ears, “The place is too cramped for me. Make room for me so that I can live here.”
You will say in your heart, ‘Who bore these children for me? I was childless and a widow. Who raised these children for me? I was left alone. Where were these children of mine?’”
This is what the Lord says: “Look, I will raise my hand to the nations and raise my signal to the islands. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your nurses, and female rulers your caregivers and wet nurses. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust from your feet. You will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be put to shame.
Can anyone take plunder from a giant? And if someone is taken captive by force, will he be saved?
This is what the Lord said: If someone takes a giant captive, he will take spoils, and whoever takes spoils from a mighty man will be saved. But I will judge their case, and I will save my children.

Those who oppressed you will eat their own flesh and drink their own blood like new wine, and they will become drunk. Everyone will recognize that I am the one who rescues you, and who accepts me as the strength of Jacob [?].

This is what the Lord says: Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce by which I sent her away? Or to which creditor did I sell you? Look, I sold you because of your sins, and because of your lawless acts I sent your mother away.

Why did I come when there was no one? Why did I call when there was no one listening to me? Is my hand unable to rescue? Or has my ear become deaf, so that it cannot hear? Rather, your sins have stood between you and God, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so that he will not have mercy on you. Am I unable to save you? Look, in my anger I will turn the sea into a desert and make the rivers dry. Their fish will dry out because there is no water, and they will die of thirst.
I will cover the sky with darkness and make its covering like sackcloth.”

The Lord is the one who will give me a trained tongue, so that I may know the right time to speak a word. The Lord is the one who will open my ears. He appointed a morning for me, like a teacher; he gave me an ear to listen.
It was the Lord’s instruction that opened my ears. I will not disobey or talk back.
I offered my back to whips and my cheeks to blows. I did not turn my face away from humiliation and spitting.
The Lord became my helper, so I was not ashamed. Instead, I set my face like a hard rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame.
For the one who vindicated me is near. Who will bring a case against me? Let him stand against me now. Who will dispute with me? Let him come near me.
Look, the Lord is the one who will help me. Who will condemn me? Look, all of you will wear out like these garments and be eaten away as by moths.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his son. You who walk in darkness and have no light, look toward the light, trust in the name of the Lord, and rely firmly on God.

Look, all of you kindle a fire and strengthen its flame. Walk in the light of your fire and in the flame you have kindled. These things have happened to you because of me: you will lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord. Look at the solid rock you quarried and at the quarry pit you dug.
Look at Abraham your father and Sarah, who gave birth to you. For he was one man, and I called him, blessed him, loved him, and multiplied him.

As for you, Zion, I have now comforted you, and I have comforted all her deserted places. I will make all her deserted places like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of praise.
Listen, listen, my people, and you kings, pay attention to me, because a law is coming from me, and my judgment will be a light for the nations.
My righteousness will draw near quickly, and my salvation is coming forth like the light. The nations will trust in my arm. The islands are waiting for me, and they will trust in my arm.

Lift your eyes to heaven and look down at the earth. See that heaven has been established like smoke, but the earth will wear out like these clothes, and those who live on the earth will die like them. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will not fail.
Listen to me, you who know justice, my people who have my law in their hearts. Do not fear people's reproach, and do not be dismayed by their insults.
For, like a garment that wears out over time, and like wool, they will be eaten by a moth. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation for generations upon generations.
Rise, rise, Jerusalem, and put on the glory of the holy arm. Rise as in the earliest days, as in a generation of long ago. Was it not you
who dried up the sea, the water of the great deep, who made the depth of the sea a road for those who were rescued to cross?

And those who were redeemed—for they will return through the Lord—are coming to Zion with joy and everlasting gladness. Gladness and praise will be upon their heads, and joy will overtake them. Heartache has fled, along with sorrow and sighing.
I am he, I am he who comforts you. Understand who you are: you feared a mortal human being and a human child, those who have withered like grass.

And you forgot God who created you, who stretched out heaven and laid the earth's foundation. You were afraid continually, every day, before the angry face of the one who oppresses you, because he planned to destroy you. Now where is the anger of the one who oppresses you?
For when he saves, he will not stand still or delay.
For I am the Lord God, who stirs up the sea and stirs up its waves. The Lord of hosts is my name.
I will put my words in your mouth, and I will shelter you under the shadow of my hand, with which I established heaven and laid the earth's foundation. And Zion will say, “My people.”
Rise, rise, stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk the cup of anger from the Lord's hand. For you drank the cup of staggering, the cup of my anger, and emptied it.
And there was no one to comfort you among all your children whom you bore, and there was no one to take your hand among all your children whom you raised.
These two things confront you. Who will grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, famine and the sword. Who will comfort you?
Your children lie asleep at the head of every street, like a half-cooked beet, filled with the Lord's anger and rebuked by the Lord God.
Therefore listen, you who are afflicted and drunk, but not with wine.
This is what the Lord, who judges his people, says: Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, the cup of my anger, and you will no longer drink it.

And I will put it into the hands of those who mistreated you and humiliated you, who said to your soul, “Lie down so that we can pass over you.” And you spread your back on the ground for everyone passing over you.
Rise, rise, Zion, put on your strength. You too, Jerusalem, the holy city, put on your glory. The uncircumcised and the unclean will no longer pass through you.
Shake off the dust, rise up and sit down, Jerusalem. Release the bonds around your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For this is what the Lord says: You were sold for nothing, and you will not be redeemed with silver.
This is what the Lord says: “My people first went down to Egypt to live there, and he carried them off by force to the Assyrians.”

“Now, then, what are you doing here?” This is what the Lord says: “My people were taken for nothing. Be astonished and cry out!” This is what the Lord says: “Because of you, my name is continually blasphemed among the nations.”
“Therefore my people will know my name on that day, because I am the one who speaks. I am here.”

Like a season on the mountains, like the feet of someone proclaiming a message of peace, like someone announcing good things: “I will let them hear of salvation,” saying, “Zion, your God will reign over you.”
For the voices of those guarding you have risen, and they will rejoice together in your midst, because they will see face to face when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
Let the deserted places of Jerusalem cry out together with joy, because he has had mercy on her and rescued her.
And the Lord will uncover his holy arm before all the nations, and all the nations, from the ends of the earth, will see the salvation that comes through God.
Separate yourselves! Separate yourselves! Come out of there, and do not touch anything unclean. Come out from her midst and purify yourselves, you who carry the Lord’s vessels.
For you will not come out in turmoil, nor will you travel in flight. For the Lord will go before you, and the one who gathers you together is the Lord, the God of Israel.
Look, my son will understand, and he will be exalted and greatly glorified.
Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored [?] people, and your glory among people.
Many nations will likewise be astonished at him, and kings will shut their mouths, because those who were not told about him will see him, and those who have not heard will understand.
Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
We spoke before him like a little child, like a root in thirsty ground. He has no beauty or glory. We saw him, and he had neither an impressive appearance nor beauty.

Instead, his appearance was dishonored, and he was more wretched than everyone else—a man afflicted by injury and acquainted with bearing suffering. For his face was turned away; he was dishonored, and they did not value him.
He is the one who will bear our sins, and he suffers for us. Yet we regarded him as being in suffering, injury, and affliction.
But he was wounded because of our lawless deeds and bruised because of our sins. The [?] for our peace was upon him; through his wound we were healed.
We all went astray like sheep. Each person wandered on his own path, and the Lord handed him over for our sins.
He himself, because he was oppressed, did not open his mouth. Like a sheep brought to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer that makes no sound, so he will not open his mouth.
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away. Who will speak of his generation? For his life will be taken from the earth. Because of the people’s lawless deeds, he was brought to death.
I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial, and the rich in exchange for his death, because he committed no lawless deed, and there is no deceit in his mouth.
And the Lord wishes to cleanse him of his injury. If you make an offering for sin, your soul will see offspring with a long life. And the Lord wishes to take
him out of the suffering of his soul, to bring him into the light, to form him with understanding, to justify the righteous one who serves many well. And he is the one who will bear their sins.

Therefore he is the one who will inherit many, and he will divide the spoils of the strong, because his soul was handed over to death, and he was counted among the lawless. He is the one who bore the sins of many and was handed over because of their lawless deeds. They rushed at him and persecuted him; they seized him, and the Lord forgave them.

Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth! Cry out and shout, you who do not suffer labor pains, because the barren woman’s children are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband. For the Lord has said:
“Enlarge the place of your tent and that of your courtyard. Make them firm; do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your tent pegs.”
Spread out farther to the right and to the left. Your descendants will inherit the nations, and you will live in the deserted cities.
Do not be afraid because you were put to shame, and do not be ashamed because you were disgraced. For you will forget your shame forever, and you will not remember the disgrace of your widowhood.
For the Lord is the one who made you; the Lord is his name. The one who rescues you is the God of Israel. He is called upon throughout the whole earth.
The Lord did not call you as a wife who has been cast out and is disheartened, nor as a wife hated since her youth, says your God.
I abandoned you for a short time. I will have mercy on you with great mercy.
I turned my face away from you in a little anger, but I had mercy on you with everlasting mercy, says the Lord who rescues you.
Since the flood in Noah’s time, this is my name, just as I swore to him at that time not to be angry with the earth or with you from now on, nor to bring a mountain against you with a threat.
Nor will your hills be moved. In the same way, my mercy will not fail you, and the covenant of your peace will not change. For the Lord has said that you are safe.
You who are humbled and troubled, whom no one has comforted—look, I will prepare your stones as rubies and your foundations as sapphires.
I will make your walls of jasper, your gates of crystal stones, and your surrounding wall of choice stones.
All your children will be taught by God, and your children will have great peace.
You will be built in righteousness. Keep away from oppression, and you will not be afraid. Terror will not come near you.
Look, converts are coming to you through me, and they will run to you.
Look, I will not create you like a blacksmith who blows on his coals and brings out his tool for his work. But I did not create you for destruction, to destroy you.

I will not allow any handmade weapon to be raised against you. Every voice that rises against you in judgment—you will cut them all down. Those who are guilty against you will be in it. There is an inheritance for those who serve the Lord, and you will be righteous before me, says the Lord.
You who are thirsty, go to the water. You who have no money, go and buy for yourselves, and eat and drink wine and milk without money or payment.
Why will you buy with money, and why is your labor spent on satisfaction? Listen to me and eat good things, and your soul will be nourished with good things.
Pay attention with your ears and follow my ways. Listen to me so that your soul may live amid good things. I will establish an everlasting covenant with you, the sure holy things of David.
Look, I have made him a witness to the nations and a ruler who commands the nations.
Nations that do not know you will call upon you. Peoples that do not know you will run to you because of your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you. Seek God.
And when you find him, call upon him at the time when he comes near you.
Let the ungodly person abandon his ways, and the lawless person his plans. Let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him, for he will abundantly forgive your sins.
For my plans were not like your plans, and my ways were not like your ways.
But just as heaven is far from the earth, so my way is far from your way, and your thoughts from my thoughts.
For just as snow or rain comes down from heaven and does not return until it waters the earth and makes it produce and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to eat,
so it is with my word that comes out of my mouth. It will not return until every word I have spoken is fulfilled, and I will make my ways and my commands straight.
For you will come out with gladness, and you will be led with joy. For the mountains and hills will leap, looking toward you with joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their branches.
A cypress will grow in place of the thornbush, and a myrtle in place of the nettle. The Lord will become a name and an everlasting sign, and he will not delay.
This is what the Lord says: Maintain justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation is near to coming, and my mercy is near to being revealed.
Blessed is the person who does these things and holds firmly to them, who keeps my Sabbaths without defiling them and keeps his hands from committing acts of violence.
Do not let the foreigner who has drawn near to the Lord say, “Perhaps the Lord will separate me from his people.” And do not let the eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
These are the things the Lord says to the eunuchs who keep my commandments, choose what I desire, and hold firmly to my covenant:
