“I will bring them to my holy mountain, and in my house and within my wall I will give them a choice place and a reputation better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not perish.”

And the foreigners who draw near to the Lord to serve him and to love the Lord’s name, to become his male and female servants, and those who keep my Sabbaths without defiling them and hold firmly to my covenant—

I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them rejoice in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.
The Lord who gathers the scattered people of Israel says, “I will gather a congregation to him.”
All you wild beasts, come and eat! All you beasts of the field, come!
Look! They have all become blind; they have not learned to understand. They are all mute dogs, unable to bark, dreaming in their sleeping places and loving to doze.
They are dogs blind in their souls, who do not know how to be satisfied. They are wicked people who do not know wisdom. They have all followed their own ways, each according to his own manner.

Look how the righteous person has perished, and no one takes it to heart. Righteous people are taken away, and no one pays attention, for the righteous person has been taken away from the presence of violence.
His burial will be in peace. He has been taken away from their midst.
But you, come here, you children of lawless people, offspring of adulterers and a prostitute!
In what have you reveled? Against whom have you opened your mouths, and at whom have you stuck out your tongues? Are you not children of destruction, offspring of lawlessness,
who invoke idols beneath shady trees, who slaughter their children in the valleys among the rocks?
That is their portion; that is their inheritance. You poured out libations to those things and offered sacrifices to them. Shall I not be angry over these things? says the Lord.
Your bed is on a high and lofty mountain, and you offered a sacrifice there.
You placed a memorial behind a royal door, thinking, “If you distance yourself from me, you will gain more.” You loved those who slept with you.
You increased your prostitution with them and multiplied those far away from you. You sent messengers beyond your borders, and you turned and humbled yourself greatly, as far as the underworld.
You grew weary on your many roads, but you did not say, “I will give up.” Now I will find strength, because I have done these things. For this reason you did not plead with me.

Before whom did you tremble and become afraid, so that you lied to me? You did not remember me or keep me in your thoughts or in your heart. I too, when I see you, will look away, and you did not fear me.
I too will declare my righteousness and your evils, which will not benefit you.

When you cry out to them, let them save you in your distress! For the wind will carry them all away, and a breeze will scatter them. But those who trust in me will acquire the land for themselves and inherit my holy mountain.
And they will say, “Clear the roads before him, and remove the stumbling blocks from the way of my people.”

These are the things the Lord says, the exalted one who dwells in the heights forever, the holy one among the holy ones, whose name is the Lord, the exalted one who rests among the holy ones, who gives endurance to the fainthearted and gives life to those whose hearts are crushed:
I will not punish you forever, nor will I always be angry with you. For a spirit comes out from me, and I am the one who made every breath.
“I grieved him a little because of sin, and I struck him and turned my face away from him. He grieved and walked sorrowfully before me in his ways.
I saw his ways and healed him. I comforted him and gave him true consolation.”
Peace upon peace to those far away and those nearby. And the Lord said, “I will heal them.”
But the sea will toss the oppressors about like this, and they will be unable to rest.
“There is no joy for the ungodly,” said the Lord God.
Cry out powerfully and do not hold back. Raise your voice like a trumpet. Tell my people their sins and the house of Jacob their lawless deeds.

They seek me day after day and desire to know my ways, like a people who have practiced righteousness and have not abandoned the judgment of their God. Now they ask me for a just judgment, and they desire to draw near to God.

They say, “Why have we fasted, but you have not looked at us? Why have we humbled our souls, but you have not noticed?” For on the days of your fasting, you pursue your own desires and oppress those subject to you.
You fast for lawsuits and fights, and you strike those who are downtrodden. Why do you fast for me in this way today, so that I may hear your voice shouting?

This is not the fast I have chosen, nor is it a day for a person to humble his soul. Nor is it a matter of bending your neck like a ring and spreading sackcloth and ashes beneath you. You must not call this an acceptable fast.
“This is not the fast I have chosen,” said the Lord. “Instead, loosen every bond of injustice, untie every knot of unjust dealings, release those who are crushed, and tear up every unjust document.”
Share your bread with the hungry, and bring the poor who have no home into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe them, and do not neglect the members of your own family.
Then your light will rise in the early morning, and your healing will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will carry you.
Then you will cry out, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking, he will say, “Here I am,” if you remove from among you bondage, plotting, and complaining speech.
Give your bread to the hungry from your heart, and have mercy on an afflicted soul. Then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will become like midday.

Your God will be with you at all times, and you will be satisfied as your soul desires. Your bones will grow strong and become like a watered garden and like a spring whose water has never failed. Your bones will flourish like a plant and grow strong, and they will inherit generation after generation.
They will rebuild your deserted places forever, and your foundations will endure forever, through [?] upon [?]. They will call you the builder of walls, and you will restore the roads in their midst.

If you do not turn your foot away from my Sabbaths, refraining from doing what you desire on the holy day, and call my Sabbaths the holy delights of your God, you must not turn your foot toward work or speak an angry word from your mouth.
You will trust in the Lord, and he will raise you up over the good things of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
Is the Lord’s hand unable to save, or has his ear become deaf so that he cannot hear?
Rather, your sins stand between you and God, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so as not to have mercy on you.
For your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with sins. Your lips have spoken lawlessness, and your tongue devises injustice.
No one speaks the truth, and there is no just judgment. They trust in chaff and speak empty things, conceiving trouble and giving birth to what is worthless.
They have hatched snakes’ eggs and are weaving a spider’s web. Whoever is going to eat their eggs breaks them open and finds a spoiled egg, with a basilisk inside it.
Their web will not become clothing for them, and they will not cover themselves with their works, for their works are lawless deeds.
Their feet run toward evil, hurrying to shed blood. Their thoughts are foolish thoughts. Destruction and misery are on their roads.
They have not known the way of peace, and there is no justice on their roads. For the roads they walk on are crooked, and they do not know peace.
Because of this, justice has withdrawn from them, and righteousness will not reach them. They waited for light, but darkness came upon them. They hoped for brightness, but walked in gloom.

They will grope along the wall like a blind person, and they will fumble like those who have no eyes. They will fall at noon like those in the middle of the night. Like those about to die, they will groan.
Like a bear and like a dove, they will walk together. We will wait for justice, but it is not there. Salvation has gone far away from us.
For our lawlessness is great before you, and our sins have stood against us. For our lawless deeds are within us, and we have recognized our sins.
We have acted unjustly and lied, and we have stopped following God. We have spoken unjust things and disobeyed. We have conceived and pondered words of injustice in our hearts.
And we pushed justice back, and righteousness went far away, because truth has failed in their streets, and they could not proceed by an upright path.
They have taken away the truth, and he turned his mind away from understanding. The Lord saw it, and it did not please him, because there was no justice.
He saw, and look, there was no one. He paid attention, and there was no one to support him. He delivered them with his arm and strengthened them with his mercy.
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and placed a helmet of salvation on his head. He put on a garment of vengeance, and his wrath
As repayment, he will repay his enemies with disgrace.

Those in the western regions will fear the name of the Lord, and those where the sun rises will fear the honored name of the Lord. For wrath comes from the Lord like a violent river; it comes with fury.
And the deliverer comes for Zion, and he will turn wrongdoing away from Jacob.

And this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My Spirit that is upon you and my words that I have put in your mouth will not depart from your mouth or from the mouth of your descendants. For the Lord has spoken, from now and forever.
Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for the light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
For look, darkness and gloom will cover the earth over the nations. But the Lord will rise upon you, and his glory will appear upon you.
Kings will walk in your light, and nations in your brightness.
Lift up your eyes all around and see all your children gathering. Look, all your sons have come from far away, and your daughters are being carried on their shoulders.
Then you will see and be afraid, and be amazed in your heart, because the wealth of the sea will turn toward you, as will that of the nations and peoples, and they are coming to you,

herds of camels. The camels of Midian and Ephah will cover you. They all come from Sheba, bringing gold, and they will bring you frankincense and precious stone, and proclaim to you the salvation of the Lord.

All the sheep of Kedar will gather to you, and the rams of Nebaioth will come to you. They will offer an acceptable gift upon my altar, and my house of prayer will be glorified. For my house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.
Who are these flying toward me like these clouds and like doves with their young? It is Samaria.

And the islands have waited for you, and the ships of Tarshish are first to bring your children to you from far away, with their gold and silver, because of the holy name of the Lord, and so that the Holy One of Israel may be glorified.
And foreigners will build your walls, and kings will stand by you. Because of my wrath I struck you, and because of mercy I loved you.
And your gates will be open at all times, day and night. They will not be shut, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought in to you, with their kings being led in.
For the nations and kings that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be utterly devastated.
And the glory of Lebanon comes to you, with cypress, pine, and cedar together, to glorify my holy place.
And the children of those who humiliated you, and those who provoked you, will come to you in fear. They will call you the city of the Lord, Zion, the holy one of Israel.
Because I had left you behind and hated you, and there was no one to help you, I will make you rejoice forever, a joy for generations upon generations.
You will suck the milk of the nations and consume the wealth of kings. You will know that I am the Lord who saves you and delivers you, the God of Israel.

And instead of bronze I will give you gold, and silver instead of iron. Instead of wood I will give you bronze, and iron instead of stones. I will establish your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
From now on, violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction or misery within your borders. Instead, they will call your walls Salvation and your gates Carved Work.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon light you at night. Instead, the Lord will be your light forever, and God will be your glory.
For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fade. For the Lord God will be your light forever, and the days of your mourning will come to an end.
And all your people will be righteous, and they will inherit the land forever—the one who protects the planting, the works of his hands, for glory.
The small one will become thousands, and the least will become a great nation. I am the Lord; I will gather them together at the proper time.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. Because of this, he anointed me and sent me to proclaim good news to the humble, to heal those whose hearts are broken, to proclaim release to captives and restored sight to the blind,
to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord and a day of repayment, to comfort all who mourn,

to give glory instead of ashes to those who mourn over Zion, and an anointing of joy instead of mourning to those who mourn, and a robe of glory instead of a sorrowful spirit. They will be called generations of righteousness, the Lord's planting, for glory.

And they will rebuild the places that have long been deserted. They will raise up what was destroyed in earlier times and renew the deserted cities and the places that have been ruined for generations upon generations.
Strangers will come and tend your sheep, and foreigners will be your farmers and vine growers.
But you will be called priests of the Lord, servants of God. You will consume the resources of the nations, and they will marvel at you amid their wealth.
This is how they will inherit the land a second time, with everlasting joy upon their heads.
For I am the Lord, who loves righteousness and hates robbery committed through violence. I will give their labor to the righteous, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring and their children will be known among the nations. Everyone who sees them will recognize that these are the offspring blessed by God.

And they will rejoice greatly in the Lord. Let my soul rejoice in the Lord, for he has clothed me in a garment of salvation and a robe of joy. He has placed a turban upon me like a bridegroom and adorned me with ornaments like a bride.
And as the earth makes its flowers grow, and as a garden makes its seeds grow, so the Lord will cause righteousness and rejoicing to spring up before all the nations.
I will not remain silent for Zion's sake, and I will not stop for Jerusalem's sake, until my righteousness comes forth like light and my salvation burns like a torch.
And the nations will see your righteousness, and kings your glory. You will call yourself by your new name, the name by which the Lord will call you.
And you will be a beautiful crown in the Lord's hand and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
From now on they will no longer call you Forsaken, and they will no longer call your land Deserted. For they will call you My Desire, and your land The Inhabited Land.
And as a young man lives with a virgin, so your children will live with you. And as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so the Lord will rejoice over you.
And I have appointed guards for you upon your walls, Jerusalem. All day and all night they will never remain silent, continually remembering the Lord.
For there is no one like you, if Jerusalem is set right and made a source of pride upon the earth.

The Lord swore by his glory and by the strength of his arm: “From now on I will never give their grain and their food to their enemies, and from now on no foreigner will drink their wine, for which you have labored.”
But those who gather them will eat them and bless the Lord, and those who gather them will drink them and eat them in my holy courts.
Go in through my gates. Prepare a road for my people and throw away the stones on the road. Raise a signal for the nations.
For look, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion, “Look, your Savior is coming to you. His reward is in his hand, and his work is before him.”
And he will call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord. But you will be called the city that is sought after and has not been abandoned.
Who is this coming from Edom, with his clothes red, from Bozrah, so beautiful, walking in a robe and with strength? “It is I, speaking in righteousness and with a judgment of salvation.”
Why are your clothes red, and your garments like those from a winepress?
“It is full and has been trampled, and there was no one from the nations with me. I trampled them in my anger and melted them like earth. I poured their blood down onto the ground.
For the Lord’s day of repayment has come upon them, and the year of redemption has come.
I looked, and there was no helper. I paid attention, and there was no one to support him. My arm saved them, and my anger stood firm.
I trampled them in my wrath and poured their blood down onto the ground.”

I remembered the Lord’s mercy and his virtues in all the things the Lord will repay us. The Lord is a good judge for the house of Israel. He will bring upon us according to his mercy and according to the abundance of his righteousness.
And the Lord said, “Are they not my people, children who will not reject me?” And he became their salvation.

From every affliction, it was not an envoy or a messenger, but he himself who saved them, because he loves them and had compassion on them. He himself redeemed them, took them to himself, and lifted them up all the days forever.
But they disobeyed and grieved the Holy Spirit. And the Lord turned against them in hostility; he himself fought against them.
And he remembered the days of old, the one who brought the shepherd of the sheep up from the land, the one who placed the Holy Spirit within them,
the one who brought Moses up at his right hand, the arm of his glory. This is how he brought your people. He made the water stand firm before him, to make an everlasting name for himself.
He brought them out through the deep like a horse through a desert, and they did not struggle.
And like livestock through a plain, a spirit came down from the Lord and led them. This is how you [?] your people, to make a glorious name for yourself.

Look down from heaven. Turn, Lord, from heaven, and look from your holy dwelling and your glory. Where are your zeal and your strength? Where is the abundance of your mercy? For you have held back from us, Lord.
For you are our Father, because Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us. But you, Lord, are our Father. Save us; from the beginning your name has been upon us.
Why, Lord, have you led us astray from your way? You have hardened our hearts so that they do not fear you. Return for the sake of your servants, for the sake of the tribes of your inheritance,
for you possessed a little on your holy mountain.
We have become as we were at first, when you did not rule over us and your name was not called upon us.

If you open heaven, trembling will seize the mountains because of you, and they will melt as wax melts before a fire. The fire will burn the enemies, and the Lord’s name will be revealed among the enemies. The nations will be shaken before you.
Whenever you do glorious things, trembling will seize the mountains because of you.
From ancient times we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen, another God besides you, or your works that you will do for those who wait for you.
For mercy will meet those who practice righteousness, and they will remember your ways. Look, you became angry with us, Lord, and we sinned; because of this we went astray.

We have all become like unclean people, and all our righteousness is like a cloth stained with menstrual blood. We have withered like leaves because of our lawlessness; this is how the wind will carry us away.
No one calls on your name or remembers to take hold of you, for you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
Now, therefore, Lord, you are our Father. We are the clay, all of us the work of your hands.
Do not be excessively angry with us, and do not remember our sins forever. Instead, turn back, Lord, because we are all your people.
Zion, the city of your holy place, has become a wilderness, and Jerusalem has become like deserted places.
Our holy house has become a curse, and the glory that our fathers praised has been burned. All the honored places have fallen.
Despite all these things, you held back, Lord, and you remained silent, and you humbled us greatly.
The Lord said, “I revealed myself to those who were not seeking me. I was found among those who were not asking about me. I said to the nation that had not called on my name, ‘Look, here I am!’”
I stretched out my hands all day to a disobedient and defiant people, who walk on a path that is not good, but have followed their sins.
These people provoke me to anger right before my eyes. They offer sacrifices in gardens and burn incense on bricks to demons that do not exist.
They sleep in tombs and graves to have dreams. They eat pork and broth from sacrifices. All their vessels are polluted.
They say, “Stay away from me! Do not come near me, because I am holy.” This is the smoke of my anger; a fire will burn among them every day.
Look, they are written before me. I will not remain silent until I repay into their laps
their sins together with their fathers’ sins, says the Lord. These are the ones who burned incense on the mountains and provoked me to anger on the hills. I will repay their deeds into their laps.

This is what the Lord says: Just as a grape is found in its cluster, and people say, “Do not destroy it, because the Lord’s blessing is in it,” so I will act for the sake of those who are my servants. For this reason I will not destroy them all.
I will bring forth descendants from Jacob and from Judah, so that they may inherit my holy mountain. My chosen ones and my servants will inherit it and live there.
There will be sheepfolds in the wooded land, and the valley of Achor will be a resting place for the cattle of my people who sought me.
But you who abandon me and forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for the demon and fill the mixing bowls for Fortune,

I will deliver you all to the sword. You will all fall by the sword, because I called to you and you did not listen. I spoke, and you ignored me. You did evil before my eyes and chose the things I do not want.

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: “Look, my servants will eat, but you will go hungry. Look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.”
Look, my servants will celebrate with joy, but you will scream because of the pain in your hearts, and you will cry out because your spirits are broken.
For you have left the Lord’s name behind you as a curse for my chosen ones. But the Lord will kill you, and my servants will be called by a new name.

This is what they will bless on the earth, for they will bless the true God. Those who swear oaths on the earth will swear by the true God. For they will forget their former suffering, and it will not come to mind.
For heaven and earth will become new, and people will not remember the former things, nor will they come to mind.
Instead, they will find joy and celebration in it. For look, I will make Jerusalem a celebration and my people a joy.
I will celebrate over Jerusalem and rejoice over my people. The sound of weeping and the sound of screaming will no longer be heard in it.

No short-lived person will be there, nor an old person who does not complete their lifespan. For the little child will reach a hundred years, and the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and will be cursed.
They will build houses and live in them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit and drink their wine.

They will not build houses for others to live in, nor will they plant for others to eat. For the days of my people will be like the days of the tree of life. They will carry out the works of their labors [?].
My chosen ones will not labor in vain, nor will they bear children under a curse, because they are offspring blessed by God.
And before they cry out, I will listen to them. While they are still speaking, I will say, “What is the matter?”

Then wolves and lambs will graze together. The lion will eat straw like the ox, and the snake will eat earth like bread. They will not act violently or destroy anything on my holy mountain, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What house will you build for me, or where is my resting place?”
“For my hand made all these things, and all these things are mine,” says the Lord. “And whom will I look upon except the humble and the contrite person who trembles at my words?”

“But the lawless person who slaughters an ox for me is like someone who kills a dog. Someone who offers fine flour to me is like pig’s blood. Someone who offers incense as a memorial is like someone who blasphemes. They have chosen their own ways, their deceit, and their abominations—the things their souls desired.”

“I too will choose their mockeries and repay them for their sins, because I called them and they did not listen to me. I spoke, and they did not pay attention. They did evil before me and chose the things I do not desire.”

Listen to the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his word. Say to those who hate you, “Our brothers,” and to those who detest you, so that the Lord’s name may be glorified and he may appear in their joy, and those people may be put to shame. When the Lord comes in his joy, then these people will be put to shame.
The sound of a cry from a city! The sound from the Lord’s temple, as he repays those who oppose him!
Before the woman in labor gives birth, before the pain of labor comes, she is delivered and bears a male child.

Who has heard of such a thing, and who has seen anything like this? Has a woman gone into labor in a single day, or has a nation been born all at once? For Zion went into labor and gave birth to her children.
“But I gave this expectation, and you did not remember me,” says the Lord. “Look! Was it not I who made both the woman who gives birth and the barren woman?” says the Lord.
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and celebrate, all of you who live in her. Rejoice with joy, all of you who mourned over her.
So that you may come in, nurse, and be satisfied from her comforting breast; so that you may drink milk and delight yourselves from the [?] of her glory.

For this is what the Lord said: “Look! I will direct the glory of the nations toward them like a river of peace, and like rushing floodwater carrying the glory of the nations. They will carry their children on their shoulders and comfort them on their knees.”
“For just as a mother comforts someone, so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.”
You will see, and your heart will rejoice. Your bones will flourish like growing grass. The Lord’s hand will be revealed to those who serve him, and he will bring it down upon those who disobey him.
For look! The Lord is coming like fire, and his chariots like a whirlwind, to repay with vengeance in anger and with rebuke in a flame of fire.
For the whole earth will be judged by the Lord’s fire, and all flesh by his sword. Many will be slain by the Lord.

Those who consecrate themselves and purify themselves for the gardens, and those who eat pig’s flesh at the doorways, along with abominations, mice, and unclean things, will perish together, says the Lord.
“And I know their deeds and their thoughts. I am coming to gather all nations and languages, and they will come and see my glory.”

And I will set a sign upon them, and I will send those among them who have escaped to the nations—to Tarshish, Put, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, and Greece, and to the distant islands that have not heard my name or seen my works and my glory. And they will proclaim my glory among the nations.

And they will bring your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord God, with horses, chariots, mule-drawn carriages, and canopies, to Jerusalem, the holy city, says the Lord, just as the children of Israel make offerings to me with joy and psalms at the house of the Lord.
I too will take some of them for myself as priests and Levites, says the Lord.
For just as the new heaven and the new earth that I will create remain before me forever, says the Lord, so your descendants and your name will endure, says the Lord.
And it will happen, month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath, that all people will come before me to worship in Jerusalem, says the Lord God.
They will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and all people will look at them.
